For they persuade themselves that the choice of men must not be neglected, nor the degrees of wickedness confused, but that there must be proportion, as it seems to them, between fault and punishment.

units.la: 4. Creatoris quinetiam sapientiam & bonitatem decere statuunt, ut distinctionem specierum animatium conseruare, sic principum creaturarum, quæ rationa-les sunt, ac ad Dei imaginem initio conditæ, commodis & incolumitati sic consulere, ut ne eadem, qua bruta, conditione esse uideantur: ac in primis, ut bene sit bonis & veritatem amantibus, male aut sit malis, &c.
units.tr: 4. They further hold that the wisdom and goodness of the Creator require him to preserve the distinction between the species of living things, and likewise to provide for the advantages and safety of the chief of creatures, which are rational and were originally made in the image of God, so that they do not appear to be in the same condition as the brute beasts; and above all that it go well with the good and those who love the truth, and ill with the wicked, and so on.

units.la: 5. Accū Deus sit veritas & summe ἐπι-χαριτάτος, æquum illis videtur, ἐπιχαριτάνων osorum veritatis contundi, nō aut successibus & oppressione testium veritatis augeri & confirmari.
units.tr: 5. Since God is truth and supremely [ἐπιχαριτάτος] gracious, it seems right to them that the enemies of the truth be crushed, not that the truth be increased and confirmed by the successes and oppression of its witnesses.

units.la: 6. Et quia oppressa veritate, Deum contumelia affectum iri persuasum habent, nolut eius hostes unquam superiores videri: cum tamen Dei opera inter media contraria fiant, & uiatrix veritas, palmæ in more pressa, assurgat & emineat, fuoq; fulgore oculos Sophistarum perstringat, docilium mentes illustret.
units.tr: 6. And because they are persuaded that, if the truth is oppressed, God will be affronted, they are unwilling that his enemies should ever seem to have the upper hand. Yet God's works are done amid contraries, and the truth, pressed down like a palm under a weight, rises up and stands out, and with its light dazzles the eyes of the Sophists and illumines the minds of the teachable.

units.la: 7. Verentur enim, ne hostes veritatis tot successibus confirmati, nihil reliqui faciant ad exstirpandam veritatem, & omnes eius assertores plane exstinguendos. Atqui non ex eo, quod Deus hominum ingratitudinem ulciscens, veritatis vexillum aliquandiu subducit, recte colligitur, nunquam illud in publicum quasi postliminio reducendum esse.
units.tr: 7. For they fear that the enemies of the truth, strengthened by so many successes, will do nothing to root out the truth and will utterly extinguish all its defenders. But it does not follow rightly, from the fact that God, avenging men's ingratitude, withdraws the banner of the truth for a while, that it should never be brought back into the open as if by right of return.

units.la: Ἀντιφάσεων [?] istarum cogitationum, quæ pijs semper in numerato esse debent. Quæ sint dolorum istorum remedia: & errorum, qui illos excitant, ἀλεξιφάρμακα[?] κα[?], paucis accipite.
units.tr: [Antitheses] of these thoughts, which ought always to be ready to hand for the pious. Hear briefly what the remedies for these griefs are, and the [ἀλεξιφάρμακα [?]] antidotes to the errors that stir them up.

units.la: 1. Cùm ἀντιλογία[?] Sophistarū sit testimo-nium stantis à partibus nostris veritatis: animū nobis addere, nō deijcere debet.
units.tr: 1. Since the contradiction of the Sophists is a testimony that the truth stands on our side, it ought to add courage to us, not cast us down.

units.la: 2. Omnis castigatio in præsens quidem non videtur esse gaudij, sed tristiciæ: ac postea fructum tranquillum iusticiæ reddit ijs, qui per eâ fuerint exercitati. Hebræorum 12.11.
units.tr: 2. Every castigation seems at the present time not to be a matter of joy but of sorrow, yet afterwards it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it. Hebrews 12:11.

units.la: 3. Dei est, non nostrum, delectum hominum & recte ac secus factorum & horum omnium specierum & graduū, verbo factisq; constituere: non autem piorum, curiose in Dei iudicia inquirere, eaque praeiudicij lance expendere. Nos enim facile labimur in pronunciando: Deus vero semper recte pronunciat & agit, nec unquam fallitur aut fallit.
units.tr: 3. It is God's business, not ours, to judge men and to determine by word and deed what is rightly or wrongly done, and of all these kinds and degrees. It is not for the pious to pry curiously into God's judgments and weigh them on the scales of prejudice. For we easily slip in pronouncing judgment, but God always judges and acts rightly, and is never deceived nor deceives.

units.la: 4. Etiamsi omnia sursum deorsum vol-ui & confundi nobis videantur: tamen in medijs tenebris & confusionibus luce & distinctionem mirandam, bonorumq; felicitatem, malorum infelicitatem, ideo statuere oportet, quia Deus est iudex mundi, cuius providetia omnia ad fines suos ducuntur.
units.tr: 4. Even if everything seems to us turned upside down and confused, yet we must hold, in the midst of darkness and confusion, that there is a wonderful light and distinction, and that good men are blessed and the wicked unhappy, because God is the judge of the world, by whose providence all things are led to their ends.

units.la: §. Cum autem Deus, ueritatem & piorum praeconio, & impiorum ἀντιλογίας [?] illustrari, uelit: ut illorum trepidatio nimia corrigenda, sic horum ἐπιχειρηματίας [?] minimè diuturna aut felix uincenda est.
units.tr: §. Since God wills that the truth be illustrated by the proclamation of the pious and by the contradictions of the impious, his excessive alarm must be corrected in the one case, and in the other the attempts of these men must be overcome as being by no means lasting or fortunate.

units.la: 6. Saepenumerò veritas prella multò magis emergit, quàm cum securos habet praecones. Ac eius precium feré magis æstimatur pro sua dignitate, cum sunt qui ea erepta, mendacia sua substituere conantur.
units.tr: 6. Very often the truth emerges far more brightly when it is attacked than when it has secure proclaimers. And its worth is generally more highly esteemed according to its dignity when there are those who try to snatch it away and substitute their own lies.

units.la: 7. Neq; verò, quò Sophistae respiciant, sed quid illis permittat Deus, & quid Ec clesiae suae promiserit, nobis præcipuè est spectandum. Sinit Deus aliquandiu fanaticos homines suas ἐπιβοδιαδακναλίας [?] ἢ ἀγνοφωνίας [?], velut longam telam texere & retexere: ut monent certamina Arianorum, Eutychianorum & aliorum. Atque id facit, ut mundus poenas det impietatis & iniusticiae: & ut pijs non desint necessaria exercitia fidei, invocationis, constantiae, vigilantiae, & aliarum virtutum. Interea, signa sua, cum res postulat, Ecclesiae suae cospicienda sistit, & subministrat Prophetas: Psal. 74.9. ac veritatis vexillum altius attollit, ut ad illud ij confugiant, qui φιλαλλήλων[?] cum φιλαδελφία coniun-xerunt.
units.tr: 7. Nor indeed should we chiefly look to what the Sophists regard, but to what God permits them and what he has promised to his Church. God allows fanatical men for a time to weave and unweave their long web of [ἐπιβοδιαδακναλίας [?]] or [ἀγνοφωνίας [?]], as the conflicts of the Arians, the Eutychians, and others show. And he does this so that the world may pay the penalty of impiety and injustice, and so that the pious may not lack the necessary exercises of faith, of invocation, of constancy, of watchfulness, and of other virtues. Meanwhile he sets up his signs, when the situation requires, to be seen by his Church, and supplies prophets: Psalm 74:9. And he raises the banner of the truth higher, so that those who have joined love of one another with love of the brethren may flee to it.

units.la: Vt autem uos, fratres charissimi, per sanctum Christi nomen oro, ut ad caetera pietatis exercitia addatis preces & curā religiosam de Ecclesia: & ut obseruetis eos, qui disidiorum & scandalorum auctores sunt, & ab eis declinetis: ita uos hortor, ut de euentu istorum certaminum, si Ecclesiam spectetis, & de uictoria bene persuasi, uos ipsos in tristitiae tentatione erigatis, & animos uestros obfirmetis, ne frangantur & deijciantur. Dabit enim Deus, pro infinita sua bonitate, fine pijs & ueritatem amatibus exoptatum. Haec de Capite primo dicere uisum est, ad Dei gloriam, & nostram institutionem. Vos, quae recte dicta sunt, Deo: caetera humanae ignorantiae & infirmitati, accepta ferentes: una mecum Deum orabitis, ut porro quoq; nobis adef-fe uelit.
units.tr: But I beg you, dearest brethren, by the holy name of Christ, that along with the other exercises of piety you add prayers and a religious care for the Church, and that you watch those who are the authors of dissensions and scandals, and keep away from them. So I exhort you, that if you look to the Church and are well persuaded of the outcome of these conflicts and of victory, you lift yourselves up under the temptation of sorrow and strengthen your minds, lest they be broken and cast down. For God, in his infinite goodness, will grant to the pious and to those who love the truth the end they desire. These things seemed fit to say about the first chapter, to the glory of God and for our instruction. You, who receive what has been rightly said as from God, and the rest as due to human ignorance and weakness, will pray to God with me that he may also be pleased to be with us henceforth.

units.la: CAPUT SECUNDUM Habacuc Prophetæ.
units.tr: CHAPTER 2 OF THE PROPHET HABAKKUK.

units.la: EXstat in Annalibus Cedreni narratio, de quodam uiro sancto, qui cum temporibus Phocæ, ἀλάστορος potius q Imperatoris, Deum ad disceptationem provocans, quæsiuisset: Ἰὼ, διὰ τί τοιοῦτον κακο[?] φανόμου βασιλέα ἀδικοῦντας: Domine cur adeo impium Regem dedisti? audiuit uocem, cum quidem neminem uideret, sibi dicē-tem: Deteriorem alium inueniri potuis-se nullum: atque hoc meruisse Constan-tinopolitanorum flagitia.
units.tr: In the Annals of Cedrenus there is an account of a certain holy man who, in the times of Phocas (a demon rather than an emperor), challenged God to a debate and asked: "Oh, why do you let a king who appears so wicked do such wrong?" [Ἰὼ, διὰ τί τοιοῦτον κακὸν φαινόμενον βασιλέα ἀδικοῦντας;] Lord, why have you given us so wicked a king? He heard a voice, though he saw no one, saying to him that no worse man could be found, and that the Constantinopolitans had deserved this for their crimes.

units.la: Quid uero aliud nobis hac tempestate, confusiones imperiorum, & Religionis depravationes, & pericula quæ nobis ab impijs Mahometistis, & ab aliis hostibus impedent, deploratibus, Deum re-spondere αὐτῷ τῷ [illegible, ~4 letters] dicemus, quam peccata nostra multo maiores pœnas mereri, quam sint eæ quas publicè priuatimq; grassari querimur?
units.tr: What else, then, will we say God answers when, in these times, we lament the upheavals of empires, the corruption of religion, and the dangers that the impious Mahometans and other enemies threaten us with, than that our sins deserve far greater punishments than those we complain of, publicly and privately?

units.la: Cur autem sic nostris doloribus indul-gemus, ut interim ea, quæ & nobis priuatim, & toti Ecclesiæ honori, solatio & usui esse possunt, nō satis consideremus, nec etiam recte æstimemus? Atqui non solum quid mali, sed etiam quid boni rebus nostris insit, spectandum erat: & mala quidem corrigenda pro virili, bona aut agnoscenda erant, & eorum auctor Deus celebrandus.
units.tr: Why, however, do we indulge our sorrows so much that we do not sufficiently consider, nor rightly weigh, those things which can serve our private consolation and use, and the honour of the whole Church? Yet we ought to look not only at what evil is in our affairs but also at what good is in them: evils should be corrected as far as we can, and goods should be acknowledged, and God, their author, should be praised.

units.la: i. Lucet, inæstimabili Dei dono, Euangelij lux, quam Sol iustitiæ Iesvs Christvs, Antichristianis tenebris pulsis & dissipatis, his postremis temporibus, accedit. Nec post tempora Augustini, Hieronymi, Ambrosij & aliorum, qui [illegible, ~8 letters] fuerūt, tanta fuit perspicuitate tradita Ecclesię doctrina in floretissimis & cultissimis ciuitatibus & provincijs, quanta nunc traditur etiā in obscuris quibusdā pagis.
units.tr: i. The light of the Gospel shines, a gift of God beyond all price, which Jesus Christ, the Sun of righteousness, has brought in these last times, the Antichristian darkness having been driven off and scattered. Since the times of Augustine, Jerome, Ambrose and the others who were (there was none) the teaching of the Church has never been delivered with such clarity as it is now delivered, even in certain obscure country villages, let alone in the most flourishing and cultivated cities and provinces.

units.la: 2. Diuinitus etiam excitati & illustrati sunt quidam lucidissimi φωστῆρες & docto res Ecclesiæ, qui docendo, Scripturas diuinas interpretando, & cum hostibus veritatis differendo, plantant & rigant ar-vum Dei, incremento largiente Domino.
units.tr: 2. Some most brilliant lights and teachers of the Church have also been raised up and enlightened by God, who, by teaching, by interpreting the divine Scriptures, and by disputing with the enemies of the truth, plant and water the field of God, while the Lord gives the increase.

units.la: Quis etiam non videat, triarijs regni Pō-tificij, & inter alios Turriano, illustrem ἀνταγωνιστήν[?] oppositum à Domino exercituum, qui unus multorum instar est, ac DispuDisputationibus suis κατασκευαστικοῖς[?] ἢ ἀνασκευαστικοῖς[?], sic ueritatis caussam aduersus mendaciorum asseclas tuetur, ut Sophi-stis unà cum armis elabendi uias adimat & praecludat: ueritatem autem amantibus ἀληθὴς[?] fit, & quo pacto bona caussa bene fit agenda, νουθετικῶς[?] doceat?
units.tr: Who does not also see that, among the champions of the Papal kingdom, Turrianus is an illustrious opponent, set against him by the Lord of hosts, who is in himself worth many? By his disputations, both constructive and destructive, he so defends the cause of truth against the followers of lies that he takes away and cuts off the Sophists' ways of escape, together with their weapons. And how is it that a good cause is to be well pursued, he teaches, in a manner true to those who love the truth and in a way that admonishes?

units.la: 3. Prodeunt etiam in lucem multi praeclari libri & exegetici, quibus illustratur scripta Prophetarum & Apostolorum, quae eduntur à uiris linguarum & dicendi artium scientia, & ubertate doctrinae praestantibus. Horum scripta testantur, Ecclesias nostras Prophetis & Apostolis συμφωνοῦντας[?], & esse alienas ab omni ἐτεροδοξία-ἀκολία[?] & idololatria.
units.tr: 3. Many distinguished and explanatory books also come to light, which illuminate the writings of the Prophets and Apostles. They are published by men outstanding in their knowledge of languages and the arts of expression, and in the richness of their learning. Their writings bear witness that our Churches agree with the Prophets and Apostles, and are remote from every heterodoxy and idolatry.

units.la: 4. Etsi autem non mediocriter turbatur pax Ecclesiae, πολεμικοῖς[?] quorundam hominum scriptis: ueritas tamen impugnata magis elucet & emergit: nec etiam desunt, Dei beneficio, qui ueritati contradicentium ora obstruunt, & meretriciam laruam fucosis scriptis detrahunt.
units.tr: 4. Although the peace of the Church is not a little disturbed by the polemical writings of certain men, the truth, attacked, shines out all the more and emerges. Nor, by God's goodness, are there lacking those who stop the mouths of those who contradict the truth, and strip the harlot's mask from her with their painted writings.

units.la: 5. Videmus etiam, ingeniosam iuuentutem multis in locis diuinitus excitari ad seriam cognitionem cotrouersiarum de religione: nec προσωπολημψία[?] (eorum qui ideo posterioribus curis locum nō dant, quia uerentur,ne iacturam honorum, facultatum, gratiae summorum hominum, facere cogantur)admodum moueri: nec altera parte non audita pronunciandum iudicare. De bona parte piae & eruditae iuuentutis loquor.
units.tr: 5. We also see that, in many places, gifted young people are being raised up by God to a serious study of the controversies about religion. Nor are they much moved by partiality (of those who therefore give no place to later cares, because they fear they may be forced to lose honours, property, or the favour of the great). Nor do they think it right to pass judgment without hearing the other side. I speak of the good part of pious and learned youth.

units.la: 6. Iam uerò, ut unum hoc, quod est ὡς λιτικὸν[?], addam, quis homo intelligens, &c πολιτικῇ σοφίᾳ[?] instructus, non uidet, ditinitus[?] à ceruicibus nostris arma rabiemq; Turcica repelli, Germaniae haec ocia concedi, piis studijs alicubi saltem hospitia cōcedi, Antichristianorum dolos & uim infringi?
units.tr: 6. Now, to add this one thing, which is political: what intelligent man, instructed in political wisdom, does not see that by God's will the arms and the fury of the Turks have been driven back from our necks, that these leisures have been granted to Germany, that a refuge has been granted to godly studies at least somewhere, and that the wiles and power of the Antichristians have been broken?

units.la: Nihil iam de aliis diuinae benedictionis formis, quae ab inexhausta bonitate in Ecclesia redundant, dicam: sed hoc potius, & mihi & uobis, charissimi fratres, à Christo Iesu Domino nostro precabor, ut nobis quoq; det id quod noster Prophe-ta, à Spiritu sancto edoctus & animatus, se facturum, in cap.2.v.1. his uerbis prosi-tetur:
units.tr: I will say nothing now of the other forms of divine blessing which overflow in the Church from inexhaustible goodness. But rather, dear brothers, I will pray this to Christ Jesus our Lord, both for myself and for you: that he may also grant us that which our Prophet, taught and animated by the Holy Spirit, professes in chapter 2, verse 1, that he will do, in these words:

units.la: Super custodiam meam stabo, & confi-stam super munitionem, atq; cōtemplabor, ut ui
units.tr: I will stand upon my watch, and station myself upon the fortress, and I will look out, that I may see

units.la: ut nideā[?] quid loquatur in me (Dominus) & quid respondeam arguenti contra me.
units.tr: what the Lord will say in me, and what I shall answer when he reproves me.

units.la: PHRASIVM DECLARATIO.
units.tr: DECLARATION OF THE PHRASES.

units.la: 1. Super custodiâ suâ stare. Existimo esse allusionem ad simile de speculatoribus, quod Ezechiel Propheta toto fere capitę 33. exposuit. Vsus est eodem simili Ifaias, cap. 52 & 56. Super custodiam suam stare dicuntur, qui gnauiter sacro suo munere defunguntur, totiq; in eo sunt, ut pro animabus sibi concreditis excubent. Ἐμφασις[?] aute est in uerbo Stare, quod idem quod religiose alicui seruire, significat.
units.tr: 1. To stand upon one's watch. I think this is an allusion to the similar image of watchmen, which the Prophet Ezekiel set out in nearly the whole of chapter 33. Isaiah used the same image in chapters 52 and 56. Those are said to stand upon their watch who carry out their sacred office diligently and are wholly intent on keeping watch for the souls entrusted to them. The emphasis lies in the word "stand," which means to serve someone with devotion.

units.la: 2. Consistere super munitionem. Plena est dulcissimæ cŏfolationis hæc phrafis, quæ monet[?], pios quidē doctores nunquā non in magno uersari discrimine, sed tamen eos Dei manu sic protegi, ut nō magis tuti esse potsint in munitisimis locis. Iuxta illud: Ecce ego dedi te hodie in ciuitatem munitá, & in columnam ferreá, & in murum æreum super omnem terrá, Regibus Iuda & Principibus eius, sacerdotibus eius, & populo terræ. Etipsi quidem pugnabūt contra te, sed nō prę-uale-bunt bunt tibi: quia tecū sum, dicit Iehouah, ut liberem te. Ier.i.v.18.19.
units.tr: 2. To station oneself upon the fortress. This phrase is full of the sweetest comfort. It reminds us that godly teachers are indeed always in great danger, but are so protected by God's hand that they cannot be safer even in the most fortified places. Compare: "Behold, I have made you this day a fortified city, and an iron pillar, and a bronze wall, against all the land, against the kings of Judah, its princes, its priests, and the people of the land. They will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, for I am with you, says Jehovah, to deliver you." Jer. 1:18–19.

units.la: 3. Contemplari & uidere quid loquatur Dominus: id est, accuratè obseruare, quid tum dictis, tum factis testetur Dominus. Ad hanc diligentiam uoce diuina inuitamur, Psal. 46.9. Venite, uidete opera Iehouae, &c. E diametro repugnat isti phrasi, contemplari quid faciat, aut quid polliceatur caro. Eius consequens est, mittere ad iniquitate manus suas. Psal.125.3.
units.tr: 3. To look out and see what the Lord will say: that is, to observe carefully what the Lord attests, both by his words and by his deeds. We are invited to this diligence by the divine voice, Ps. 46:9: "Come, see the works of Jehovah," etc. The opposite of this phrase is to look at what the flesh does or promises. Its consequence is to "send forth one's hands to iniquity." Ps. 125:3.

units.la: 4. Respondere Domino argueri. Quàm hoc fit ἀδύνατον,[?] liquet ex illo Iobi dicto: Verè noui ita rem habere, & quomodo iustificabit se homo cum Deo? Si uelit cōtendere cum eo, non respondebit ei ad u-num ex mille. Sapiens corde est, & fortis robore: quis dura loquetur ei, & erit in pace? Iob.9.2.3.4.
units.tr: 4. To answer the Lord when one is reproved. How impossible this is appears from that saying of Job: "Truly I know it is so; but how can a man be just before God? If he wishes to contend with him, he cannot answer him one in a thousand. He is wise in heart and strong in power; who has hardened himself against him and prospered?" Job 9:2–4.

units.la: Eleganter autem, ut beatus Hieronymus inquit, & miro sensu humanam describit impatientiam, quam in disceptationibus semper habere consueuimus: ut antequam aliquis nobis exaduerso respondeat, & sciamus in quo nos arguerit, ad respondendum paremur. Ex quo osten-ditur, responsionem nō rationis esse, sed contencontentionis. Si enim effet ratio,respon-sio debuerat expectari: & sic uidere,utrū respondere deberet, an consentire ratio-nabili responsioni. Sed & hoc notādum ex eo quod dixerat, ut uideam quid loquatur in me: propheticam uisionem,& eloquium Dei, non extrinsecus ad Prophetas fieri, sed intrinsecus & interiori homini respondere. Unde & Zacharias: Et Angelus, inquit, qui loquebatur in me. Et in Psalmis: Audiam quid loquatur in me Deus. Et paulo superius: Itaque quia Propheta est, & propterea quærit, & dubitare se dicit: ut quod illi responderent, respondeatur omnibus. Hæc Hierony-mus.
units.tr: But Jerome, as the blessed man says, describes human impatience elegantly and with remarkable insight, the impatience we are always accustomed to show in disputations: before anyone opposes us face to face, and before we know what he is reproving us for, we prepare ourselves to answer. From this it is shown that the answer is not one of reason but of contention. For if it were reason, the answer ought to have been awaited, and so one would see whether he ought to answer, or agree with a reasonable response. But this too must be noted from what he had said, "that I may see what he will say in me": the prophetic vision and the word of God do not come to the Prophets from outside, but speak within and answer the inner man. Hence also Zechariah: "And the angel," he says, "who spoke in me." And in the Psalms: "I will hear what God the Lord will say in me." And a little earlier: "Therefore, because he is a Prophet, he also inquires and says that he doubts, so that what they answered him may be answered to all." These are the words of Jerome.

units.la: Quid ergo hac oratione sibi vult Ha-bacucus Propheta?
units.tr: What, then, does the prophet Habakkuk mean by this prayer?

units.la: Sibi, ἐν τειῷ[?] λογισμῷν[?] stanti, & summa cum admiratione intueti successus & felicitatem impiorum, & piorum ab illis op-pressorum miserias: post ἔκστασιν[?] suam, qua in disceptatione cum Deo usus erat, reue-renter petendum & exspectandum diui-num responsum, & cum nihil sit quod arguenti Deo iure obijci possit, eius iudi-cio summa cum religione standum: ac illud aliis piis bona fide exponendum es-se, ut etiam aliorum institutioni consu-latur.
units.tr: He means this for himself: standing in his reasoning [ἐν τῷ λογισμῷ] and, with great wonder, gazing on the success and prosperity of the wicked and the miseries of the pious whom they oppress; that after his ecstasy [ἔκστασιν], which he underwent while disputing with God, he must reverently seek and await the divine answer; that since there is nothing with which God, who is the judge, can rightly be charged, his judgment must be accepted with the utmost reverence; and that he must set this out in good faith to other pious people, so that the instruction of others is also served.

units.la: DE OFFICIO SERVI DEI, quem urit prosperitas improborum, [illegible, ~8 letters] quaedam.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE OFFICE OF THE SERVANT OF GOD, whom the prosperity of the wicked burns, [illegible] certain things.

units.la: 1. Ne sic commoueatur, ut etiam de sta-tione sua deserenda cogitet: sed pedem figat in custodia sua.
units.tr: 1. He should not be so moved as even to think of abandoning his post, but should plant his foot firmly in his watch.

units.la: 2. Contempletur ἡσυχῶς[?], quid tum dictis, tum factis loquatur Dominus.
units.tr: 2. Let him quietly ἡσυχῶς consider what the Lord says, both in his words and in his deeds.

units.la: 3. Etiam atque etiam perpendat, an ne & quid Iehouae argueti sit respondendū.
units.tr: 3. Let him weigh again and again whether there is anything he must answer to Jehovah when he contends with him.

units.la: Praestabit autem ista, si, Asaphi Prophetæ exemplo, ingressus in sanctuaria Dei, intellexerit nouissima tum piorum, tum impiorum: Psal 73.17. Nam si hos spectes, in lubricis ponit eos Dominus, & deijcit eos in praecipitia: sic ut vastati momento cessent, consumti ab horroribus: eodem Psalmo v.18.19. At si illos consideres, occurrit Davidis apophthegma: Contemplare integrum, & considera rectum homine: certè finis huius hominis est pax. Psal.37.v.37.
units.tr: He will achieve this if, following the example of the prophet Asaph, he enters the sanctuaries of God and understands the final ends both of the godly and of the wicked (Ps. 73:17). For if you look at the wicked, the Lord sets them on slippery ground and casts them down into precipices, so that in a moment they are destroyed and consumed by terrors (the same Psalm, vv. 18–19). But if you consider the upright, David's saying comes to mind: "Mark the blameless man and behold the upright, for the end of that man is peace" (Ps. 37:37).

units.la: Rectè etiam fecerit, si in illa disceptatione malit modestiam & φιλομαθῶς[?] in cognocognoscenda Dei uoluntate, & fidei obedientiam in eadem adprobanda, declarare, quàm iudicij acumen & ἀγχίνοιαν [?] in disceptando: & si malit Dei[?], summè sapientis & summè boni, quàm suo ipsius iudicio, stare: fitq; alijs auctor, utidem faciant.
units.tr: He will also do well, in that dispute, to prefer to show modesty and a love of learning φιλομαθῶς in coming to know God's will, and obedience of faith in accepting it, rather than keenness of judgment and quickness of wit in arguing. And if he prefers to stand by the judgment of God, who is supremely wise and supremely good, rather than by his own judgment, he will be an authority for others to do the same.

units.la: VERSVS II.
units.tr: VERSE II.

units.la: IIII. Responsio Iehouae, de pijs & improbis, & de utrorumque sorte: cuius initium occurrit v.2.cap.2. desinit autem in fine eiusdem capitis.
units.tr: 4. The response of Jehovah concerning the godly and the wicked, and concerning the lot of each. Its beginning is at v. 2 of chapter 2, and it ends at the end of the same chapter.

units.la: Respondit autem mihi Iehouah, & dixit: Scribe uisionem, & explana in tabulis, ut percurrat qui legerit eam.
units.tr: And Jehovah answered me and said: Write the vision and make it plain upon tables, that he who reads it may run.

units.la: His uerbis attentionem & fidem flagitat Dominus, dum non audiri solum, sed etiam literis mandari uult oraculu, quod in illa uisione seruo suo aperturus erat, ut institutioni legentium seruire posset.
units.tr: By these words the Lord demands attention and faith, since he wishes the oracle he was about to open to his servant in that vision not only to be heard but also to be committed to writing, so that it might serve the instruction of those who read it.

units.la: Solet magnitudo & acerbitas dolorum, attonitos reddere, & aciem mentium hebetare: ideo Dominus exsuscitat animum serui sui, & eum attente, quae dicerentur, expendere iubet.
units.tr: The greatness and bitterness of griefs usually stun the mind and dull the edge of its attention. Therefore the Lord rouses the spirit of his servant and bids him weigh carefully what is said.

units.la: Attentionis autem caussae hae erant:
units.tr: The reasons for this attention were these:

units.la: 1. Quòd oraculum effet θεόπνευστον, ὡς τιμὴ λυχνιον.
units.tr: 1. Because the oracle was divinely inspired [θεόπνευστον], as a lamp is precious [ὡς τιμὴ λυχνιον].

units.la: 2. Quòd esset in uisione diuina patefa-ctum. ἀπονεκλυψις.
units.tr: 2. Because it was disclosed in a divine vision [ἀποκάλυψις].

units.la: 3. Quòd ut ἀξιομνημόνευτον literis esset mandandum. Expositio.
units.tr: 3. Because it was to be committed to writing as worth remembering [ἀξιομνημόνευτον]. Exposition.

units.la: 4. Quòd multorum piorum institutio-ni destinatum esset. Finis.
units.tr: 4. Because it was destined for the instruction of many godly people. Purpose.

units.la: Sedenim cum ὑπόθεσις nihil habeat dif-ficultatis, ex ea occasione sumta, de uer-bo Dei scripto, & de eius auctoritate, ali-quid dicemus, in gratiam eorum qui Theo-logiae studio animum appulerunt. Idem enim iudicium est de unius partis, quod de totius Scripturae diuinae, auctoritate & usu, &c.
units.tr: But since the subject matter presents no difficulty, I shall take the occasion it offers to say something about the written Word of God and its authority, for the sake of those who have devoted themselves to the study of theology. For the judgment concerning the authority and use of one part is the same as concerning the authority and use of the whole of divine Scripture, and so on.

units.la: DE VERBO DEI SCRIPTO, Aphorismi.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE WRITTEN WORD OF GOD, Aphorisms.

units.la: 1. Scripturae Canonicae auctor Deus est.
units.tr: 1. The author of Canonical Scripture is God.

units.la: Ideo Paulus Apostolus γραφὴ θεόπνευ-στος vocat, 2. Tim. 3. 16. Non enim hominis libidine allata est olim Prophetia, sed a-cti à Spiritu sancto locuti sunt sancti Dei homines. 2. Pet. 1. 21.
units.tr: Therefore Paul the Apostle calls it "God-breathed Scripture" [γραφὴ θεόπνευστος], 2 Tim. 3:16. For prophecy was never brought forth by the will of man, but holy men of God spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. 2 Pet. 1:21.

units.la: 2. Amanuenses autem eius fuerunt sancti Dei homines.
units.tr: 2. Yet the amanuenses of God were holy men of God.

units.la: Id liquet ex Petri Apostoli testimonio, quod iam adduxi. Ac quod de voce docentium dixit Christus: Qui vos audit, me audit: Luc.io.i6. idem & de eorundem scriptis dici potest. Loquor de Prophetis & Apostolis.
units.tr: This is clear from the testimony of the Apostle Peter, which I have already cited. And what Christ said of the voice of teachers, "He who hears you hears me," Luke 10:16, can also be said of their writings. I am speaking of the Prophets and Apostles.

units.la: 5. Agit autem de Deo, eiusq; operibus & voluntate.
units.tr: 5. Scripture treats of God, and of his works and will.

units.la: Deum nemo unquam vidit: Filius autem unigenitus, qui est in sinu Patris, ille nobis exposuit. Ioan.1.18. Quid autem exposuit nobis? Haec duo, Creationem universorum, cui addi debet gubernatio: & Adoptionem nostrā gratuitam, ac protectionem. Psal.100.3. Haec ut recte cognosci possent, tradita est integra doctrina de Deo creatore & redemtore: deque Hominis creatione, lapsu, instauratione, ac restitutione in integrum.
units.tr: "No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him to us," John 1:18. But what has he declared to us? These two things: the creation of all things, to which governance must be added; and our free adoption, and protection, Ps. 100:3. So that these might be rightly known, the complete doctrine was handed down concerning God as Creator and Redeemer, and concerning the creation of man, his fall, his restoration, and his restitution to integrity.

units.la: 4. Scopus Scripturae est, Dei gloria & hominum salus.
units.tr: 4. The goal of Scripture is the glory of God and the salvation of men.

units.la: Talem enim nobis Deu[?] Scriptura canonica describit, qualis ille est, unum essentia, trinum personis, summè sapiente, bonum, iustum, misericordem, &c. Ac si nos respicias, Omnis Scriptura divinitus inspirata est, & utilis ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad institutiotutionem quæ est in iusticia: ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonû perfecte instructus. 2. Tim. 3. 16. 17.
units.tr: For canonical Scripture describes God for us as he is: one in essence, three in persons, most wise, good, just, merciful, and so on. And if you look to us: "All Scripture is divinely inspired and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, so that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work," 2 Tim. 3:16, 17.

units.la: 5. Auctoritas Scripturæ diuina est, non humana.
units.tr: 5. The authority of Scripture is divine, not human.

units.la: Etsi Ecclesia custos est librorum propheticorum & apostolicorum, ac eius est nos docere qui libri Canonici, qui Apocryphi semper habiti sint: tamè omnis Scripturæ auctoritas pendet ab auctore Deo, qui est αὐτόπιστος [?] & ἀψευδής [?].
units.tr: Although the Church is the guardian of the prophetic and apostolic books, and it is her task to teach us which books have always been held as canonical and which as apocryphal, nevertheless the whole authority of Scripture depends on God its author, who is self-trustworthy [αὐτόπιστος] and cannot lie [ἀψευδής].

units.la: Augustinus: Hic, inquit, prius per Prophetas, deinde per seipsum, postea per Apostolos, quantum satis esse iudicauit, locutus, etiam Scripturam condidit, quæ Canonica nominatur, eminetissimæ auctoritatis, cui fidem habemus de ijs rebus, quas ignorare non expedit, necper nosipsos nosse idonei sumus. lib. ii. de Ciuitate Dei, cap. 3.
units.tr: Augustine: "He," he says, "having first spoken through the Prophets, then through himself, afterwards through the Apostles, as far as he judged sufficient, also established the Scripture which is called canonical, of most eminent authority, in which we place faith concerning those things which it is not expedient for us to be ignorant of and which we are not fit to know by ourselves." Book 2 of The City of God, chapter 3.

units.la: 6. Non solum autem pijs legenda, sed etiam accurate perscrutanda est.
units.tr: 6. Scripture must be not only read by the godly but also searched out with care.

units.la: Luc. 16. 29. Habent Mosen & Prophetas: audiant illos. Ioan. 5. 39. Scrutamini Scripturas. Hoc autem est ἀνακρίνειν τὰς γραφάς [?], Act. 17. 11.
units.tr: Luke 16:29: "They have Moses and the Prophets; let them hear them." John 5:39: "Search the Scriptures." This is to examine the Scriptures [ἀνακρίνειν τὰς γραφάς], Acts 17:11.

units.la: 7. Nisi tamen Christus mentem Scripturarum aperiat, intelligi non possunt: Ideo dicitur aperire & interpretari Scripturas, Luc.24.27.32.
units.tr: 7. Unless Christ opens the mind of the Scriptures, they cannot be understood; therefore it is said that he opens and interprets the Scriptures, Luke 24:27, 32.

units.la: 8. Scriptura solide intellecta, non est Scriptura.
units.tr: 8. Scripture, if solidly understood, is not Scripture.

units.la: Hic aphorismus exstat apud beatum Theodoretum. Nos ne stolide intelligamus Scripturas, eas ἀναγίνωσκ ἡ συμβιβάζειν discamus, recte uidelicet dijudicantes & conferentes inter se & res & sententias. Hanc diligetiam Deus in postremo lemmate versus 2.Ab.2.postulat.
units.tr: This aphorism occurs in the blessed Theodoret. Lest we understand the Scriptures foolishly, let us learn to read them [ἀναγινώσκειν] and to compare them [συμβιβάζειν], that is, rightly judging and comparing with one another both the matters and the sentences. God requires this diligence in the last line of verse 2 of Hab. 2.

units.la: Deum Patrem Domini nostri Iesv Christi toto pectore oro, ut nobis det religiosè in Scripturis diuinis uersari, & eas recte συμβιβάζειν, ut per nos Dei nomen sanctificetur. Amen.
units.tr: I pray with all my heart to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ that he grant us to dwell in the divine Scriptures reverently, and to compare them rightly [συμβιβάζειν], so that through us the name of God may be sanctified. Amen.

units.la: VERSVS III.
units.tr: VERSE III.

units.la: Nam adhuc uisio erit in tempus (id est, executio naticinij istius differetur in suum tempus) & loquitur in finem (id est, cum sit uerum, suo tempore complebitur ipsis sa ctis) nec mentietur (hoc est, nec erit inane terriculamentum impijs, nec vana erunt promissiones de conseruatione & defensione piorum.) Si moram fecerit(subaudi, Iehouah, qui utetur ad rem tantam conficiendam instrumentis sibi probatis) exspecta eum, quia veniendo veniet (id est, certo veniet) & non tardabit.
units.tr: "For the vision is yet for an appointed time" (that is, the fulfilment of this prophecy will be deferred to its own time); "and it speaks toward the end" (that is, since it is true, it will be fulfilled in its own time in the facts themselves); "and it will not lie" (that is, it will not be an empty scare to the wicked, nor will the promises of preservation and defence of the godly be in vain). "If it tarries" (understand: Jehovah, who will use instruments proved fit for so great a task), "wait for it, because coming it will come" (that is, it will certainly come), "and will not delay."

units.la: Est in hoc versu προκαταληψις[?]. Etsi huius grauissimae Prophetiae de poenis populi Iudaici & vicinarum Gentium, complementum aliquandiu differtur: tamen diuinitus praefinito tempore certo complebitur, actum cognoscent omnes non tardasse Dominum.
units.tr: In this verse there is a prolepsis [προκαταληψις]. Although the fulfilment of this most grave prophecy concerning the punishments of the Jewish people and of the neighbouring nations is deferred for some time, nevertheless at a divinely predetermined time it will certainly be fulfilled, and all will recognise that the Lord did not delay.

units.la: Occurrit autem Dominus vanae imaginationi τῆς φλυαρίας[?] eorum hominum, qui fascinati humanorum praesidiorum consideratione & fiducia, opinabantur, Prophetarum comminationes, quarum executio differretur, inane murmur & brutum esse fulmen.
units.tr: But the Lord meets the vain imagination [τῆς φλυαρίας] of those men who, bewitched by their confidence in human protections, supposed that the Prophets' threats, whose execution was deferred, were an empty murmur and a dumb thunderbolt.

units.la: Tales illusores, homines φιλήδονοι[?], non φιλόθεοι[?], extremis hisce diebus venturos, & disturos: Ubi est pollicitatio adventus eius? Petrus Apostolus praenunciauit, 2. Pet. 3, 3. & sequentibus versibus. Dominus IESUS det, ne vana illorum garru-litalitate moueamur, sed uigilates exspe&te- mus Domini nostri Iesv Christi ad- uentum,lumbis præcinctis & lucernis ar- dentibus.
units.tr: Such scoffers, lovers of pleasure [φιλήδονοι], not lovers of God [φιλόθεοι], would come in these last days and say, "Where is the promise of his coming?" as the Apostle Peter foretold, 2 Pet. 3:3ff. May the Lord Jesus grant that we not be moved by their idle chatter, but, waiting watchfully for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, keep our loins girded and our lamps burning.

units.la: Sic autem argumentatur Dominus(o- ftendens cauendum pijs paralogifmum fecundum nō caussam ut caussam : Deus non eueftigiō dispensat præmia & pœ- nas. Igitur eius denunciationes sunt ful- gur è pelui : ut aiunt) κατὰ βῖωμ,
units.tr: But the Lord argues in this way (showing that the godly must beware of the paralogism which takes what is not the cause for the cause: God does not carry out rewards and punishments at once; therefore his threats are a bolt from a clear sky, as they say) "in the customary manner" [κατὰ βίωμα].

units.la: Non debet uana & mendax haberi il- la uisio,cuius complementum etsi differ- tur,tamen diuinitùs determinato tempo- re & modo uerè complebitur. Talis au- tem est hæc uisio de aduetu hostium Ba- byloniorum & impressione in Iudæam. Quare non debet uideri uana, &c. Hæc breuiter de ὑποθέσι monere uisum est: su- perest ut ad πρᾶξιν, quam Thesis indicat, accedamus.
units.tr: That vision should not be regarded as vain and false, whose fulfilment, though deferred, will nevertheless truly be accomplished by God at a determined time and in a determined manner. Such is this vision concerning the coming of the Babylonian enemies and their assault upon Judah. Therefore it should not be seen as vain, and so on. These things have been thought fit to be briefly noted concerning the hypothesis; it remains that we come to the practice [πρᾶξις], which the Thesis indicates.

units.la: DE MORA DIVINA, QVAM PIOS boni consulere decet.
units.tr: On the Delay of God, Which the Godly Ought to Take in Good Part.

units.la: Prudentiæ uidetur esse, fecundum il- lud uetus di&tum : τὸ σύμφορον μέλει μοι, τὸ δ' ἀνήκον τῆς οἰκίας: Hodierna dies, & quæ nunc præstò sunt, mihi cordi sunt: quis scit quid cras futurum fit? præfentia tantùm curare, & indigné ferre, si quod iá u-sui esse poterat, differatur. Iuxta distichó:
units.tr: It seems the mark of prudence, according to that old saying, "What is expedient is my concern, and what belongs to the household" [τὸ σύμφορον μέλει μοι, τὸ δ' ἀνήκον τῆς οἰκίας], that today and what is now at hand should be our concern. Who knows what tomorrow will bring? To attend only to present things, and to take it badly if what could already have been used is put off. As the couplet has it:

units.la: ὠκέαι χαρίτες γλυνκόπικρον ἀλί βραδυλύωιπᾶσαι χαρίτες ὑμνῖν, μὴ δὲ λέγοιτο χαρίς.
units.tr: Swift are the graces, bittersweet, but slow to loosen; all graces are hymned, and let not grace be spoken of [ὠκέαι χάριτες γλυνκόπικρον ἀλί βραδυλύωι πᾶσαι χάριτες ὑμνῖν, μὴ δὲ λέγοιτο χάρις].

units.la: Atqui præstabat meditari aureum illud Salomonis apophthegma: Omni rei est determinatum tempus, & tempus est omni uoluntati sub cœlo. Eccles. 3.1.
units.tr: Yet it would have been better to ponder that golden saying of Solomon: "To every thing there is a time, and a season for every purpose under heaven." Eccles. 3.1.

units.la: Ansit?
units.tr: Whether It Happens?

units.la: Moram aliquando interuenire in dispensatione operum Dei, extra controuersiam esse debet. Est enim Deus agens uoluntarium. Itaque pro infinita sua sapientia, potentia, iusticia & bonitate, aliàs accelerat opera sua, aliàs differt, si, inquam, humanum spectes iudicium: nam si cõsideres Deum, is uerò omnia in tempore facit. Ac uniuersalis experientia omnium piorum, ita rem habere testatur. Iofephi à fratribus uéditi liberatio & exaltatio, totos 13. annos dilata fuit, usque ad tempus, quo uenit uerbum eius, & ser mo Iehouæ probaret eum. Psal. 105.19. Et quàm multi nostrûm, diu rebus aduersis agitati, tandem Deo nos respiciente, & in portum è tempestuoso mari deducente, experti sumus, præcipuo nostro bono dilatam latam fuisse liberationem, eam tamen tempore gratuitae Dei misericordiae nobis summa fide praestitam: Doluit iam olim multis piis tristissima perturbatio ἀλλὰ ταραχὴ[?] Ecclesiae Dei, quae excitata est vehementia & importunitate Acacianorum, suum ἀντιχριστῶν[?] obtrudentium Ecclesiae: ac optabat sane illi Christum θεάνθρωπον[?], de cuius gloria agebatur, sese sic interponere, ut totus mundus cognosceret iudicium eius. Sed Deo visum est rem diu differre, & ut suorum in fide virtutem exploraret, & ut iis qui veritate oppugnabant, amentiam suam proderent coram toto mundo, darentque poenas & spretae & oppugnatae veritatis. Itaque & nos boni consulamus duram & difficilem nostram militiam, & spe gaudetes, expectemus donec vexillum veritatis altius extollat Dominus, & se a partibus eorum, qui credunt Iesum Christum in carne venisse, stare, αὐτῷ τῷ ἔργῳ[?] testetur: id quod suo tempore haud dubie facturus est.
units.tr: That a delay sometimes intervenes in the working out of God's works ought to be beyond dispute. For God is a free agent. Therefore, by his infinite wisdom, power, justice and goodness, he sometimes hastens his works and sometimes defers them, if, I say, you look at the human judgement; for if you consider God, he does all things in due time. And the universal experience of all the godly bears witness that this is so. The deliverance and exaltation of Joseph, sold by his brothers, was deferred for thirteen years, until the time when his word came and the word of the LORD tried him. Ps. 105.19. And how many of us, long buffeted by adversity, have found, when God looked upon us and brought us from the stormy sea into harbour, that our deliverance was deferred for our greater good, yet was granted to us in God's own time, by his free mercy, with firm faith. Long ago a most grievous disturbance [ταραχή] of the Church of God, stirred up by the violence and importunity of the Acacians, who thrust their Antichristian [ἀντιχριστῶν] teaching upon the Church, troubled many godly people. They truly wished that Christ, the God-man [θεάνθρωπος], whose glory was at stake, would interpose himself, so that the whole world might know his judgement. But it seemed good to God to defer the matter for a long time, both to test the virtue of his people in faith, and to expose before the whole world the madness of those who assailed the truth, and to punish them for despising and attacking the truth. So let us also take in good part our hard and difficult warfare, and, rejoicing in hope, wait until the Lord lifts the banner of truth higher and bears witness, by the very deed [αὐτῷ τῷ ἔργῳ], that he stands on the side of those who believe that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; which he will undoubtedly do in his own time.

units.la: Quid sit?
units.tr: What It Is?

units.la: Deus tamen reuera non tardat, ut nec praecipitando accelerat quicquam: sed nostra τῇ ἀληθείᾳ[?] procrastinare videtur promissiomissionum & comminationum suarum complementum. Ideo non nostra opinione, sed Dei sapientia, in numero, pondere & mensura omnia agentis, standū nobis est. Ac sint nobis semper in conspectu aurea hæc dicta: Non est vestrum nosse tempora siue opportunitates, quas Pater in sua ipsius authoritate posuit: Actor.i.7.[?] Item: Deus condidit ex uno sanguine omne genus hominum, ut habitarent per universam superficiem terræ, ὁρίσας προστε-ταγμένας καιροὺς[?] definitis temporibus, quas præstituit, & positis terminis habitationis eorum: Act.17.26. Item: Mea est ultio, & retributio, tempore quo nutabit pes eorum: Deut.32.35.
units.tr: Yet God in truth is not slow, nor does he hasten anything by rushing; but our own reckoning [τῇ ἀληθείᾳ] seems to put off the fulfilment of his promises and threats. Therefore we must stand not by our own opinion but by the wisdom of God, who orders all things by number, weight and measure. And let these golden words always be before our eyes: "It is not for you to know the times or seasons, which the Father has put in his own authority," Acts 1.7. Likewise: "God made from one blood every nation of men, to dwell upon the whole face of the earth, and having determined [ὁρίσας] the appointed times, and the bounds of their habitation," Acts 17.26. Likewise: "Vengeance is mine, and recompense, in the time when their foot shall slide," Deut. 32.35.

units.la: Fit tamen interdum, ut etiam Sancti, in ipsa tentationis ἀκμῇ[?], de hac re hæsitent aliquandiu. ut Iobus in paroxysmo tristi-ciæ: Quare, inquit, ab Omnipotente nō essent abscondita tempora? Iob.24.1.
units.tr: Yet it sometimes happens that even the saints, at the very height [ἀκμή] of temptation, hesitate for a while over this matter, as Job did in the bitter paroxysm of his grief: "Why," he says, "were not times hidden from the Almighty?" Job 24.1.

units.la: Ideo semper in promtu habere stude-ant dulcissimam illam Iehouæ sententiā: In tempore beneplaciti exaudiui te, in die salutis auxiliatus sum tibi: Isai.49.8. Etenim per & propter Christum, quæ eo loco æternus Pater alloquitur, nos quoque, qui ipsi concorpores καὶ σύμφυτοι facti sumus, exaudimur, & liberamur ab o-mni malo: sed eo demum tempore, quod optimo consilio ab eodem definitum est.
units.tr: Therefore let them take care always to have at hand that most sweet word of the LORD: "In an acceptable time I have heard you, and in a day of salvation I have helped you," Isai. 49.8. For through and on account of Christ, whom the eternal Father addresses in that passage, we also, who have been made fellow-bodies and grafted together with him [καὶ σύμφυτοι], are heard and delivered from every evil; but only at that time which has been fixed by him by the best counsel.

units.la: Quare fit?
units.tr: Why Does It Happen?

units.la: Dignæ sunt memoria etiam Ethnicorum saniorum sententiæ, quæ monent, moram, quę interuenire interdum, & res humanas procrastinare uidetur, plurimum non raro prodesse.
units.tr: The sayings of the wiser heathen are also worth remembering, which warn that the delay that sometimes intervenes, and seems to put off human affairs, very often does much good.

units.la: Euripides dicit: ἐν τοῖς ἀναβολαῖς τῶν λυ-πῶν ἐστ' ἄκη: In ipsa mora, malorum sunt remedia.
units.tr: Euripides says: "In the very delays of sorrows there are remedies" [ἐν τοῖς ἀναβολαῖς τῶν λυπῶν ἐστ' ἄκη]: in delay itself there are remedies for evils.

units.la: Recte etiam Sophocles ait: φιλεῖ γὰρ ὀ-νείρων πρᾶγμα ἀνὴρ πράσσων μέγα. Si hoc laudi ducitur uiris cordatis, quis no multò magis idem in Deo, omnia sapientissimè moderante, commendet?
units.tr: Sophocles also rightly says: "For a man who is accomplishing a great thing is wont [to take his time]" [φιλεῖ γὰρ ... ἀνὴρ πράσσων μέγα]. If this is held to be praiseworthy in sensible men, who would not much more commend the same in God, who governs all things most wisely?

units.la: Eleganter etiam Theognis cecinit: Μηδὲν ἄγαν [?] ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἄριστος [?] ἐργμάσιν ἀνθρώπων, πολλάκις δ' εἰς ἀρετήν. [?]
units.tr: Theognis also sang elegantly: "Nothing to excess; in all human undertakings the best course often leads to virtue" [Μηδὲν ἄγαν ... ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἄριστος ... ἐργμάσιν ἀνθρώπων, πολλάκις δ' εἰς ἀρετήν].

units.la: Sedenim ut loci & professionis Theologicæ memores, per ἀνάλογον [?] ab humanis ad diuina accedamus: initiò obseruanda sunt dicta de dilatione pœnarum.
units.tr: But, mindful of our place and of our theological calling, let us proceed by analogy [ἀνάλογον] from human things to divine. First, the sayings about the deferment of punishments must be observed.

units.la: Rom. 2. 4. τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιαν ἄγει [?]: Dei benignitas (qua ductus pœnas difdiffert) ad resipiscentiam te deducit.
units.tr: Rom. 2.4: "The goodness of God leads you to repentance" [τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιαν ἄγει]: the kindness of God, which holds back punishments, leads you to repentance.

units.la: 2. Petr. 3. 9. Non tardat Dominus, qui promisit, (ut nonnulli tarditatem esse hac ducunt) sed patiens est erga nos, nolens ullos perire, sed omnes ad resipiscentiam tendere.
units.tr: 2 Pet. 3.9: The Lord does not delay in what he has promised (as some think this slowness to be), but is patient toward us, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

units.la: Porrò, quod præmiorū dispensatione attinet, illa tempore opportuno, ac definito diuinitus, instituitur. Iuxta dicta:
units.tr: Further, as regards the dispensing of rewards, these are bestowed at a fitting time, and one divinely appointed. According to the sayings:

units.la: Psal. 32. 6. Propterea quemcunque dignaris gratia tua, deprecabitur te tempore quo inueniris.
units.tr: Ps. 32.6: "Therefore everyone who is godly shall pray to you in the time when you may be found."

units.la: Psal. 9. 9. Et erit Iehouah exaltatio oppresso: exaltatio opportunis temporibus in tribulatione.
units.tr: Ps. 9.9: "And the LORD will be a refuge for the oppressed; a refuge in times of opportunity, in tribulation."

units.la: Psal. 145. 15. Oculi omnium ad te exspectant, & tu das illis cibum ipsorū tempore suo.
units.tr: Ps. 145.15: "The eyes of all wait upon you, and you give them their food in due season."

units.la: De corona gloriæ & iusticiæ Apostolus: Quod superest, ait, repositā est mihi iusticiæ corona, quam reddet mihi Dominus in illo die, iustus ille iudex: non solum autem mihi, sed & omnibus qui exspetiuerint illustrem illius aduentum. 2. Timoth. 4. 8.
units.tr: Concerning the crown of glory and righteousness the Apostle says: "Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day; and not to me only, but to all who have loved his appearing." 2 Tim. 4.8.

units.la: Quòd sit.
units.tr: That it is so.

units.la: Longè tamē aliud est de Domini mora iura iudicium feruorum fidelium & prudē tum, aliud malorum.
units.tr: Yet it is one thing to say that the delay of the Lord is a matter for the judgment of faithful and wise servants, and quite another for the wicked.

units.la: Illi enim suo munere funguntur, alimenta famulitio Domini in tempore dā tes.Hi autem in cordibus suis dicunt:χρο-νίζει ὁ λύγιος ἐλθεῖν: ac conseruos cædunt,& cum ebrijs edunt & bibunt. Matthæi 24. 45.46.47.
units.tr: For the former carry out their duty, giving food to the household of the Lord in due season. But the latter say in their hearts, "The lord delays to come" [χρονίζει ὁ κύριος ἐλθεῖν], and they beat their fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards. Matthew 24:45–47.

units.la: Quid? an'ne iudicabimus, Harmostas quosdam,conseruos suos(quasi de plau-stro eis maledicendo, dentata charta eos confodiendo, πονηροί in exilium agen-do,nulla uirtutum & fidelitatis in officio præstitæ ratione habita) ufqueadeò inhu-maniter tractaturos esse,nisi in cordibus suis diceret: Tardat Dominus noster ad-uentum? Et quis non uideat culinarum aulicarum nidore & pemmatis delica-tos Hierophantas quosdam sic deliniri & inescari,ut cum ebrijs perpotare,& cō seruos cædere malint, quàm cum his de pietatis summa συνωνοιμ instituere? Sed uidet hæc Deus, qui etiam die quo non exspectat, ueniet: & nisi prius resipiscat (quod sanè toto pectore illis opto) sepa-rabit eos,partemq; eis assignabit cum hy-pocritis. Matth.24.51.
units.tr: What then? Shall we not judge that certain governors, who abuse their fellow servants (calling them names as if from a cart, stabbing them with toothed paper, driving the wicked into exile, with no regard for the virtue and faithfulness they have shown in their office), would treat them so inhumanly unless they said in their hearts, "Our Lord is slow to come"? And who does not see that certain court hierophants, pampered by the fragrance of kitchens and the delicacies of pastry, are so soothed and enticed that they would rather drink deep with drunkards and beat servants than enter into a sworn fellowship with these men on the highest matters of piety [συνωμοσίαν]? But God sees these things, and he will come on a day when they do not expect him; and unless they first repent (which I sincerely wish for them with my whole heart), he will separate them and assign them their portion with the hypocrites. Matthew 24:51.

units.la: Nos,fratres carisimi,patientes simus, & stabiliamus corda nostra: quoniā adventus Domini appropinquat. Ne ingemiscamus alij adversus alios, ut ne condemnemur: ecce, Judex ante januam astat: Jac.5.9. Bonam autem caussam bene agamus: nec Antagonistarum more, conviciis odijsque certemus: nec abeo quod malum est,nos vinci patiamur: sed vincamus bonitate maliciam: Rom.12. versu ultimo.
units.tr: Let us, dearest brothers, be patient and strengthen our hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near. Let us not groan against one another, lest we be condemned: behold, the Judge stands before the door. James 5:9. Let us, however, carry on a good cause well, and not contend with conviction and hatred in the manner of our opponents; nor allow ourselves to be overcome by what is evil, but overcome evil with good. Romans 12, last verse.

units.la: VERSVS IIII.
units.tr: VERSE 4.

units.la: Ecce extollit se is, cuius anima non est recta in eo: Justus autem fide sua vivet.
units.tr: Behold, he who is puffed up, his soul is not upright in him; but the just shall live by his faith.

units.la: Sicut uniones & gemmæ,non magnitudine, sed precio,elegantia & aliis modis, saxa longè vincunt: ita hoc aureum dictum,mira brevitate res summas complectitur. Deus det nobis, ut illud pie ὀρθοτομίαν posimus.
units.tr: Just as pearls and gems, by their price, elegance and other qualities rather than by their size, far surpass stones, so this golden saying embraces the greatest matters in wonderful brevity. May God grant us to handle it rightly [ὀρθοτομίαν].

units.la: Propositio orationis Jehovæ, tradita in hoc versu 4, constat ἀντίθεσις Injusti & Justi: quorum ille sese extollere,id est,brevi tempore supra alios sese efferre, eminere & florere: hic autem fide sua in æ-ternum vivere,dicitur.
units.tr: The proposition of the prophet Habakkuk, set out in this verse 4, consists of an antithesis between the unjust and the just. Of these, the one is said to puff himself up, that is, to lift himself above others for a short time, to stand out and to flourish; but the other is said to live forever by his faith.

units.la: Quia uero difficilis hic locus est, & ad iustificationis negocium, ac ad exhortationem ad patientiam, adhiberi solet, primum sensum eius grammaticū exponemus: deinde propheticū sensum, ex Apostoli Pauli sententia, fideliter declarare stu debimus.
units.tr: Since this is a difficult passage, and is commonly brought forward in the matter of justification and in exhortation to patience, we must first set out its grammatical sense, and then faithfully declare its prophetic sense, following the judgment of the Apostle Paul.

units.la: Quid facturos censes Nebucadnezarem & Chaldaeos eius clientes?
units.tr: What do you suppose Nebuchadnezzar and his Chaldean clients will do?

units.la: Extollent sese ipsos maiorem in modum. nec id cuiquam mirum uideri debet, cum eorum animae nō sint rectae: sed incredulitate distortae, & à Deo auersae. Inflat enim incredulitas, cum sibi uidetur praesidijs satis instructa, & cum successus carni & sanguini gratos illa consequitur: ut exempla summorum in hoc mundo hominum testantur, Alexandri Magni, Pompeij, Marij, Sullae, & multorum aliorum: de quibus dicit Psaltes: Impius in altitudine naris suae non inquirit: omnes cogitationes eius sunt, quod non sit Deus: Psal.io.4.
units.tr: They will puff themselves up greatly, and this should seem surprising to no one, since their souls are not upright but twisted by unbelief and turned away from God. For unbelief puffs up when it seems to itself sufficiently furnished with protections, and when it obtains successes pleasing to flesh and blood; as the examples of the greatest men in this world testify: Alexander the Great, Pompey, Marius, Sulla, and many others. Of them the Psalmist says: "The wicked, in the pride of his nose, does not seek; all his thoughts are that there is no God." Psalm 10:4.

units.la: Quid aut fideles, interim dum illi emergunt & triumphant, facturos censes?
units.tr: What, meanwhile, do you suppose the faithful will do while those others rise up and triumph?

units.la: Fide sua uicturi sunt, patienter ferentes aduersos casus, & certò persuasum habentes, futurum ut Deus Ecclesiam fer-uet mirando modo. Erit etiam in silen-tio & spe, no in curribus & equis, eorum fortitudo. Ad humana praesidia necre-spicient, nec cofugient: cotenti protecti-one & gubernatione diuina, & spe gau-dentes: Rom.12.12.
units.tr: They will live by their faith, bearing adverse chances patiently, and holding firmly the persuasion that God will preserve his Church in a wonderful manner. Their strength will also lie in quietness and hope, not in chariots and horses. They will not look to human protections, nor flee to them, but will be content with the protection and governance of God and rejoice in hope. Romans 12:12.

units.la: PROPHETICA SENTENTIA.
units.tr: THE PROPHETIC SENTENCE.

units.la: Propositum nobis est, per ἀνάβασιν[?] ab hypothesi ad thesim ascendere, & uestigia Apostoli Pauli, ad patientiam nos exhortantis, pro uirili sequi. Eius autem haec uerba sunt, Hebr.10.38. Iustus autem ex fide uiuet: at si quis se subduxerit, non probat eum animus meus. 39. Nos uero non ij sumus qui nos subducamus ad exitium, sed qui credamus ad animae salutem.
units.tr: It is our purpose, by an ascent from hypothesis to thesis, to follow as far as we can the footsteps of the Apostle Paul, who exhorts us to patience. His words are these, Hebrews 10:38: "But the just shall live by faith; but if anyone draws back, my soul has no pleasure in him." 39: "But we are not those who draw back to destruction, but those who believe to the saving of the soul."

units.la: Propositionis primae expositio.
units.tr: Explanation of the first proposition.

units.la: Iustus fide sua uiuet. In hac categorica & affirmante propositione subiectum est, Iustus: praedicatum, Viuet sua fide. De his duab.partibus ordine uiderimus.
units.tr: "The just shall live by his faith." In this categorical and affirmative proposition the subject is "the just," and the predicate is "shall live by his faith." Let us consider these two parts in order.

units.la: Cum ὁμώνυμον[?] sit Iusti uocabulum, uideamus, quot modis & de quibus illud in Scripturis diuinis praedicetur.
units.tr: Since the word "just" is used equivocally, let us see in how many ways, and of what things, it is predicated in the divine Scriptures.

units.la: 1. Deus κατ' ἐξοχὴν[?] Iustus dicitur, respe[?]tu essentiæ & iudicij. Iustus enim est, & ipsa iusticia. Psal.11.7. Iustus Iehouah iusticiam diligit: rectum uidet facies eius.
units.tr: 1. God is called just pre-eminently [κατ' ἐξοχήν], with respect to his essence and his judgment. For he is just, and is justice itself. Psalm 11:7: "The LORD is righteous, he loves righteousness; his countenance beholds the upright."

units.la: 2. Fide iustificati [?]κατὰ λογισμὸν[?] Iusti dicuntur. Imputatur enim illis fides ad iusticiam: Rom.4.3. Ac de his dicitur: Oculi Iehouæ super iustos: Psal.34.15.
units.tr: 2. Those justified by faith are called just by reckoning [κατὰ λογισμόν]. For faith is imputed to them for righteousness. Romans 4:3. And of these it is said: "The eyes of the LORD are upon the just." Psalm 34:15.

units.la: 3. Hypocritæ, qui [?]κατὰ δόξαν[?] iusti sunt, æquiuocè Iusti uocantur. Matth.9.13. Non ueni uocare iustos, sed peccatores, ut resipiscant.
units.tr: 3. Hypocrites, who are just in appearance [κατὰ δόξαν], are called just equivocally. Matthew 9:13: "I came not to call the just, but sinners, that they may repent."

units.la: 4. Hyperbolicè seneri homines, qui omnia ad uiuum refecàtes, obliuiscuntur eius uulgò quod dici solet, Summum ius, summa iniuria: dicuntur Iusti itidem æquiuocè. Eccles.7.17. Ne sis iustus multum, & ne sis sapiens nimium: ut quid desolaberis?
units.tr: 4. Men who are excessively severe in hyperbole, who, reducing everything to its strictest form, forget what is commonly said: "The highest law is the highest injustice," are likewise called just equivocally. Ecclesiastes 7:17: "Be not overly just, nor overly wise; why should you destroy yourself?"

units.la: Hoc autem loco agitur de fide iustificatis, qui Dei bonitatem & omnipotentiam intuentes, in illo solo acquiescunt.
units.tr: But in this passage we are concerned with those justified by faith, who, looking to the goodness and omnipotence of God, rest in him alone.

units.la: Prædicatum est, Fide sua uiuit. Nos in lingua Germanica idiotismo, Ich gelebe der hoffnung/ crebrò utimur: qui quidem Hebraeæ [?]πίστει[?], Iustus fide uiuet, belle respondet. Sententia est: Iustus, fide intelligit, sibi nequaquam in rebus aduerfis despondendum esse animum, sed potius contra spem sub spe crededum: Roman.4.18. persecutionem sese pati,fedin ea non deseri : deijci, at nō perire : 2.Corinth.4.9. cum momentanea leuitas oppressionis excellenter æternum pondus gloriæ ipsi cōficiat,eod.cap.v.17.eoq; nomine afflictiones patienter ferendæ sint. Hoc autem ὑπομονῆς toto cap.11.Epistolæ ad Hebræos sic traͤuit Paulus,ut non fit necesse meridiem facibus admotis illustrare.
units.tr: The predicate is "shall live by his faith." We in the German language often use the idiom <bl>I live in hope</bl>, which answers well to the Hebrew [πίστει], "the just shall live by faith." The sense is this: the just man understands that in adverse circumstances his spirit must by no means be despaired of, but that he must believe in hope against hope (Romans 4:18); that he suffers persecution but is not forsaken in it, is cast down but does not perish (2 Corinthians 4:9); since the momentary lightness of the affliction works for him an exceeding eternal weight of glory (ibid., v. 17), and for this reason afflictions are to be borne patiently. Paul has set forth this patience throughout the eleventh chapter of the Epistle to the Hebrews in such a way that there is no need to light a noonday sun with torches.

units.la: Propositionis secundæ explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation of the second proposition.

units.la: Animus meus non probat eos qui se subducunt.
units.tr: My soul does not approve of those who draw back.

units.la: ὑποστέλλομενοι est, Ii qui fe subducunt, id est, qui propter incredulitatem Deo diffisi, ad humana præsidia tandem confugiunt. Vt Iudæi alias Syriæ, alias Chaldæorum, alias Ægypti Regum patrocinium και συμμαχίαν ficulnum sane præfidiū expetiuerunt, & largitionibus alijsq; modis sibi conciliare studuerunt.
units.tr: ὑποστελλόμενοι [hypostellomenoi] means those who draw back, that is, those who, distrusting God because of their unbelief, finally take refuge in human protection. So the Jews at one time sought the patronage of the kings of Syria, at another time of the Chaldeans, and at another of the Egyptians, as an alliance [συμμαχία] and a truly worthless safeguard, and they tried to win support by bribes and other means.

units.la: τὸ ὑποστελλόμενον, Animus meus nō probat. Notum est illud de Iudæis oraculū: Væ filijs declinantibus, dicit Iehouah, ut faciant consilium, & non ex me: & tegāt se tegumento, & non ex Spiritu meo, ut addant peccatum super peccatum. Qui proficiscuntur ut descendant in Ægyptu, & os meum non interrogaverunt, ut se-ipsos roborent in fortitudine Pharaonis, & sperent in umbra Ægypti. Erit autem vobis fortitudo Pharaonis in pudorem, & spes in umbra Ægypti in ignominiam, &c. Isai.3o.1.2.3. Item: Sic dicit Iehovah, Maledictus vir qui fidit homini, & ponit carnem brachium suum, & a Iehovah recedit cor eius. Erit tanquam myrica in deserto, neque videbit cum venerit bonum, sed habitabit in siccitatib. in deserto, &c. Ierem.17.5.6.
units.tr: τὸ ὑποστελλόμενον [to hypostellomenon]: "My soul does not approve." The oracle against the Jews is well known: "Woe to the children who turn aside, says the LORD, to take counsel, and not from me; and who cover themselves with a covering, and not by my Spirit, so as to add sin to sin. They set out to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth, to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh and to trust in the shadow of Egypt. But the strength of Pharaoh shall be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your disgrace," etc. (Isa. 30:1-3). Likewise: "Thus says the LORD: Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart departs from the LORD. He shall be like a juniper in the desert, and shall not see when good comes, but shall dwell in parched places in the wilderness," etc. (Jer. 17:5-6).

units.la: In versu 39.cap.10. ad Ebraeos, consolatur Paulus fideles, & ait: Nos autem non ij sumus qui nos subducamus ad exitiu, sed qui credamus ad animae salutem.
units.tr: In verse 39 of chapter 10 of Hebrews, Paul comforts the faithful and says: "But we are not of those who draw back to destruction, but of those who believe to the saving of the soul" (Heb. 10:39).

units.la: QVOMODO IDEM APOSTOLVS verba Habacuci, Justus fide sua vivet: ad ju-stificationis negocium retulerit.
units.tr: HOW THE SAME APOSTLE REFERRED THE WORDS OF HABAKKUK, "The just shall live by his faith," TO THE MATTER OF JUSTIFICATION.

units.la: Apostolus noster duobus locis verba Habacuci, quae nunc in manibus habe-mus, ad justificationem retulit: Rom.1.17. & Gal.3.11. Verba eius haec sunt: Iusticia Dei per Euangelium retegitur, ex fide in fidem. Sicut scriptum est: iu-stus autem ex fide uiuet.
units.tr: Our Apostle refers the words of Habakkuk, which we now have before us, to justification in two places: Rom. 1:17 and Gal. 3:11. His words are these: "The righteousness of God is revealed through the gospel, from faith to faith. As it is written: 'The just shall live by faith.'"

units.la: Sic argumentatur Paulus: Cuicunque tribuitur uita, eidem & iusticia, quam illa consequitur ut effectum. Vt enim peccati (quod est uniuersalis iniusticia, cum sit ἀ-νομία, 1. Ioan. 3. 4.) auctoramentū est mors, Rom. 6. 23. sic iusticia uitæ principiū est. Neq; huic sententiæ repugnat eiusdem uersus lemma posterius: Donum autem Dei est uita æterna in Christo Iesu Domino nostro. Non enim uitæ donum, citra gratuitam iusticiæ Christi imputationem, nobis confertur.
units.tr: Paul argues thus: life is given to the one to whom righteousness also belongs, as its effect follows from it. For as death is the wage of sin, which is universal unrighteousness since it is lawlessness [ἀνομία] (1 John 3:4), so Rom. 6:23, righteousness is the beginning of life. Nor does the following clause of the same verse contradict this: "But the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord." For the gift of life is not conferred on us apart from the free imputation of the righteousness of Christ.

units.la: Sed fidei (quæ uidelicet τῇ πληροφορίᾳ & certa perfuasione, de propitia Dei erga nos uoluntate, definitur) uita tribuitur. Ac prudenter sanè Bucerus in colloquio Ratisbonensi: Viuitur, dixit, fide, quia illa excipit uitam Dei, non quia ipsa eam affert.
units.tr: But life is given to faith, which is defined as full assurance [πληροφορία] and certain persuasion of God's favourable will toward us. Bucer rightly said at the Colloquy of Regensburg: "We live by faith, because it receives the life of God; not because it brings that life itself."

units.la: Rectè igitur fidei etiam iusticia, quam annunciat Euangelium, tribuitur.
units.tr: Therefore it is rightly said that righteousness, which the gospel proclaims, is also given to faith.

units.la: Contrà:
units.tr: On the contrary:

units.la: Vita est donum Dei: Rom. 6. 23. Igitur non est fidei tribuenda.
units.tr: Life is the gift of God (Rom. 6:23). Therefore it is not to be attributed to faith.

units.la: Respondeo:
units.tr: I answer:

units.la: Quæ sunt subordinata, non pugnant. Deus αὐτὸν ζωὸν[?] vitæ est: Fides causa organica est, quæ ut iustitiæ, sic etiam vitæ donum excipit. Ac vocabulorum πρὸς ἐν[?] ea ratio est, ut λαμβάνεται[?] τι instrumento id tribuatur, quod alioquin proprium est causæ efficientis principis. Sed hoc omne Paulus sapienter exposuit, Gal.2.20. Vitam quam nunc uiuo in carne, uiuo per fidem Filij Dei, qui dilexit me, & tradidit semetipsum pro me.
units.tr: Things that are subordinate do not conflict. God is the author of life; faith is the organic cause, which receives both righteousness and the gift of life. Such is the manner of speaking that what properly belongs to the principal efficient cause is attributed to the instrument. Paul wisely set out all this in Gal. 2:20: "The life I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me."

units.la: Alter locus, in quo etiam ad iustificationem uerba nostri Prophetæ à Paulo referuntur.
units.tr: The second passage, in which also the words of our Prophet are referred by Paul to justification.

units.la: Nullum autem per legem iustificari apud Deum, manifestum est: siquidem iustus ex fide uiuet. Gal.3.11.
units.tr: That no one is justified before God by the law is plain, since "the just shall live by faith" (Gal. 3:11).

units.la: Tale est argumentum Pauli, ab oppositis: Si iustitia & uita fidei tribuitur, tum certe non tribuuntur operibus. Iuxta illud: Quod si per gratiam, non iam ex operibus: alioquin gratia iam non est gratia: Rom.11.6. Item: Ideo ex fide (est hæreditas) ut sit per gratiam, ut sit firma promissio toti semini: Rom.4.16.
units.tr: Paul's argument is of this kind, from opposites: if righteousness and life are given to faith, then certainly they are not given to works. Accordingly: "But if it is by grace, it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace" (Rom. 11:6). Likewise: "Therefore it is of faith, that it may be by grace, so that the promise may be sure to all the seed" (Rom. 4:16).

units.la: Verum est Antecedens, Abac.2.4.
units.tr: The antecedent is true (Hab. 2:4).

units.la: Verum igitur est & Consequens. Hæc ut confirmentur, fideiq; officia & necessitas illustretur, indicem præcipuorum fidei attributorum nunc subiungam. Fide intelligimus Deum esse uniuersorum[?] conditorem: Hebr.11.3. In fide sumus, & Iesum Christum in nobis esse statuimus: 2.Cor.13.5. Fide viuimus in Christo: Gal.2.20. Fide uidemus Christum: Ioan.8.56. Fide edimus & bibimus Christum: Ioan.6.35. Fide incedimus: 2.Cor.5.10. Per fidem corda nostra a Deo purificatur: Act.15.9. Fide, ex fide, & per fidem iustificantur electi: Rom.3.28.30. In fide stamus: 1.Cor.16.13. Fide patrissamus[?]: Rom.4.16. Fide benedictionem consequimur cum fideli Abraham: Gal.3.9. Per fidem promissum illum Spiritum accipimus: eode cap.v.14. Fides per charitatem agit: Galat.5.6. Ideo celebratur ἔργου τῆς πίστεως[?], 1. Thess.1.3. Per fidem habitat Christus in cordibus nostris: Eph.3.17. Fide, ceu scuto, iacula mali illius ignita exstinguimus: Eph.6.16. Per fidem Euangelij uno pariter animo decertamus: Phil.1.27. In fide permanendum fundatis & firmis, ne dimoueamur a spe Euangelij quod audiuimus: Col.1.23. Fide & charitate ceu thorace utimur: i.Theff.5.8. In fide perseue- randum est: 1. Tim.2. 15. Placemus Deo fide: Hebr.11.6. Fide sequimur ducem Christū: Hebr.12.2. Fide petimus à Deo bona necessaria: Iac.1.6. Fide [illegible, ~6 letters] fata- næ resistimus: 1.Pet.5.8. Fide ædificamur, vt est in Epistola Iudæ.
units.tr: Therefore the consequent is true also. To confirm this, and to make clear the duties and the necessity of faith, I now add an index of the chief attributes of faith. By faith we understand that God is the creator of all things (Heb. 11:3). We are in the faith, and we affirm that Jesus Christ is in us (2 Cor. 13:5). By faith we live in Christ (Gal. 2:20). By faith we see Christ (John 8:56). By faith we eat and drink Christ (John 6:35). We walk by faith (2 Cor. 5:7). Through faith our hearts are cleansed by God (Acts 15:9). By faith, from faith, and through faith the elect are justified (Rom. 3:28, 30). We stand in the faith (1 Cor. 16:13). We are rooted by faith (Rom. 4:16). By faith we obtain the blessing with faithful Abraham (Gal. 3:9). Through faith we receive the promised Spirit (ibid. v. 14). Faith works through love (Gal. 5:6). Therefore the "work of faith" is praised (1 Thess. 1:3). Through faith Christ dwells in our hearts (Eph. 3:17). By faith, as with a shield, we quench the fiery darts of that evil one (Eph. 6:16). By the faith of the gospel we contend together with one mind (Phil. 1:27). We must continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, not moved from the hope of the gospel which we have heard (Col. 1:23). We use faith and love as a breastplate (1 Thess. 5:8). We must persevere in the faith (1 Tim. 2:15). We please God by faith (Heb. 11:6). By faith we follow Christ as our leader (Heb. 12:2). By faith we ask God for the good things we need (James 1:6). By faith we resist the snares of Satan (1 Pet. 5:8). By faith we are built up, as is said in the Epistle of Jude.

units.la: Addamus [illegible, ~6 letters] paucula dicta Patrum.
units.tr: Let us add a few sayings of the Fathers.

units.la: 1. Fidelis totum mundum habet, cum Deum habet, ut ait Augustinus.
units.tr: 1. The faithful man has the whole world when he has God, as Augustine says.

units.la: 2. Fides, spes, charitas, sunt spiritualis ædificij portæ, teste Gregorio.
units.tr: 2. Faith, hope and love are the gates of the spiritual building, according to Gregory.

units.la: 3. Fides vera nunquam turbatur, ut ait Ambrosius.
units.tr: 3. True faith is never disturbed, as Ambrose says.

units.la: 4. Fides nisi præcedat, bona vita sequi non potest. Idem.
units.tr: 4. Unless faith goes before, a good life cannot follow. The same.

units.la: 5. Vires fidei tetatione discutur. Idem.
units.tr: 5. The strength of faith is tested by temptation. The same.

units.la: DE FIDE IVSTIFICANTE, Methodus.
units.tr: ON JUSTIFYING FAITH: METHOD

units.la: Fidei definitionem, causas, effectus & adiuncta, methodo didascalica in gratia Iuniorum exponere, propositum nobis est. Dominum itaque Iesum fidei [?]ἀρχη- [?]γὸν oro, ut eam in nobis augeat, ad sui nominis gloriam, & omnium nostrum instaurationem; Amen.
units.tr: It is our purpose to set out, in a didactic method for the benefit of the young, the definition, causes, effects and attendant circumstances of faith. Accordingly, I pray the Lord Jesus, the beginning [ἀρχηγόν] of faith, that he would increase it in us, to the glory of his name and the renewal of us all. Amen.

units.la: I. Significationes vocabuli.
units.tr: I. The meanings of the word

units.la: Quia Fidei uocabulũ πολύσημον in Scri-pturis est, quæ'nam eius præcipua significata sint, & quid in hac propositione, Iu-stus fide sua viuet: proprie significet, ad-hibito instrumento ἀιαρετικῶ, principiô annotabimus.
units.tr: Since the word faith [Fides] is polysemous [πολύσημον] in Scripture, we shall first note, by the method of division [διαιρετικῷ], what its chief meanings are and what it properly signifies in this proposition: "The just shall live by his faith."

units.la: 1. Fides, σωτηρικῶς sumto eius uocabu-lo, significat veritatem & constantiam in dictis, factis, pactis & conuentis. In hac significatione rectissimè tribuitur Deo, Rom.3.3. Num incredulitas eorum fidem Dei inanem reddet? Absit. Item renatis hominibus, Tit.2.10. Nihil interuertetes, sed omnem bonam fidem ostendentes, ut doctrinam Seruatoris nostri ornent in omnibus.
