units.la: προσκαταλήψις[?] est: Etsi me in nassa hostili irretitum, infirmum & lentum esse, reipsa experior: tamen, cum nō in meipsum, nec etiam in hostes, sed in Deum omnipotentem, mihi respiciendum norim, nō dubito, Deum robora fesso, celeritatem tardo concessurum, ut alijs quoque decantádi laudes diuinas materiam, exemplo meo, subministrem. Notum est Isaiæ dictum: Qui dat lasso fortitudinem: & cui non sunt uires, robur multiplicat. Lassantur quidem adolescentes, & fatigantur, & iuuenes cadendo cadunt: At sperantes in Iehouah mutabunt robur: ascendent ala sicut aquilæ: current, & non lassabuntur: ambulabunt, & non fatiga-buntur. cap. 40. 29. 30. 31.
units.tr: Prokatalepsis [προσκατάληψις] is this: although I find by experience that I am caught in the enemy's net, weak and slow, yet since I know that I must look not to myself, nor even to the enemies, but to God Almighty, I do not doubt that God will grant strength to the weary and speed to the slow, so that by my example I may also supply others with matter for singing the divine praises. The saying of Isaiah is well known: "He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: but they that wait upon Jehovah shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not faint." Isa. cap. 40. 29, 30, 31.

units.la: Cæterum cum Habacuc noster ad uerbum descripserit uerba Dauidis, Psal. 18. 33.34. de quibus alias dicendum erit, finem nunc faciam.
units.tr: Moreover, since our Habakkuk has written down word for word the words of David, Ps. 18. 33, 34, about which I shall speak elsewhere, I will make an end here.

units.la: Vt autem Deo Patri, per sanctū nomen Iesu Christi filij eius unigeniti, toto pecto[?] re gratias ago, q; nobis dedit, ut Habacuci ἐξήγησιν, pro nostro qualicunq; modulo, pertexere possemus: ita eundem oro, ut nobis det gratiā sancti Spiritus sui, ut omnia hæc oracula ad institutionem & consolationem nostram dextrè adhibere possimus.
units.tr: But as I give heartfelt thanks to God the Father, through the holy name of Jesus Christ his only-begotten Son, who has granted us to work out an exposition of Habakkuk, however modest my measure may be, so I likewise pray him to give us the grace of his Holy Spirit, that we may apply all these oracles aptly to our instruction and consolation.

units.la: Amen.
units.tr: Amen.

units.la: 1581. 19. Decembris.
units.tr: 1581, 19 December.

units.la: PARAPHRASIS PSALMI DAVIDIS XXXVII, conscripta ab Adriano Borckio Pom.
units.tr: Paraphrase of Psalm 37 of David, composed by Adrian Borck of Pomerania.

units.la: Nete [?] malorum prosperæ res sobria De mente quatiant, neu bonis Horum caducis quicquam iniquus invide, Ventus levis quæ dissipat. Nam lacteus ceu floris aprici decor, Abit repente marcidus, Falce amputatus: nulla pars sic gaudii Sincera fluxi permanet. Tu sedulus sphæra in Deum, nec regula Vitæ, eius unquam ab orbita Deflectat: in terra mane, aruaq; fidei Fœcunda iugiter cole. Omnis voluptas in Deo sit, & tuis Votis benignus annuet. Quæcunq; versat animus illi credito, Et ipse faciet omnia. Operta virtus forte si fuit tua, Horum malignis artibus, Hanc mox apertam faciet, ut Solis quidem Certet corusco lumini. Deo quiesce, neu dolore ringere, Si prosperis successibus
units.tr: Let not the prosperous fortunes of wicked men shake a sober mind, and do not, unjust man, envy their fleeting goods, which a light wind scatters. For like the milky bloom of a sunny flower, it fades suddenly when the sickle cuts it down; no part of such passing joy remains pure. You, be diligent: let your orbit be toward God, and let the rule of your life never turn aside from his course. Remain in the land and continually cultivate the field of faith, which bears fruit. Let all your delight be in God, and he will graciously grant your prayers. Whatever your mind turns over, entrust it to him, and he himself will bring everything to pass. If your virtue has perhaps been hidden by their malicious arts, he will soon make it open, so that it vies with the glittering light of the sun. Rest in God, and do not fret with grief if Fortune again and again intoxicates the wicked with prosperous successes.

units.la: Fortuna prauos usq; & usq; inebriat. Tu mentem ab ira contine: Ne forte mens patrare quiduis impotens, Labatur in scelus graue.
units.tr: Fortune intoxicates the wicked again and again. Restrain your mind from anger, lest the mind, unable to govern itself, slip into some grave crime.

units.la: Nam iustus orbis arbiter delet malos: At spem locantes in Deum, Longæua terras incolent in secula, Seriscq; tradent posteris.
units.tr: For the just judge of the world destroys the wicked; but those who place their hope in God will dwell on the earth for long ages and hand it down to their posterity.

units.la: Breue ecce tempus, nusquam erunt & impij, Nec umbra uanæ gloriæ Quæsita restabit. Sed usq; exerciti Diris pij periculis,
units.tr: Behold, the time is brief: the wicked will be nowhere, and no shadow of vain glory they sought will remain. But the pious, always tried by dire dangers,

units.la: Terras in alto possidebunt otio, Et posteris linquent suis.
units.tr: will possess the lands on high in leisure, and leave them to their heirs.

units.la: Vtcunq; dente infrendat impius truci, Bonisq; construat dolos, Cladem imminentem prouidens eius Deus, Deridet irritas minas.
units.tr: Whenever the wicked man grinds his teeth in fierce rage and plots against the good, God, foreseeing their impending ruin, mocks their empty threats.

units.la: Intendit arcum, & stringit ensem, gestiens Vt maclet[?] insidijs pium: At ense proprio cadet, tum spicula Frangentur arcus noxij.
units.tr: He bends his bow and draws his sword, eager to slay the pious by ambush; but he will fall by his own sword, and the arrows of the wicked bow will be broken.

units.la: Angusta pauperum iuuat plus recula, Quæsita rectis artibus, Quàm diuitum, congesta per nefarium Scelus, superba copia.
units.tr: The narrow little possessions of the poor please more, won by upright arts, than the proud abundance of the rich, heaped together by wicked crime.

units.la: Nam conteretur fastus omnis impij, at Suos Deus tuebitur:
units.tr: For all the pride of the wicked will be crushed, but God will protect his own.

units.la: Seris & uberem parentum prorogat Hereditatem posteris. Quin intonat quando hinc & inde tristibus Fortuna laeua cladibus, Et res,& omne uita cuius indiget, His affluenter suppetent. Praui peribunt, ceu uorax uelociter Depascit ignis uictimam. Cum mutuatur impius, reddit nihil. At iustus usq; pauperum Miseritus, ipse utcunq; parce uictitet, Prodest, iuuatq;, & commodat. Hinc tanta tanq; larga praemia obtinet, Vt quisquis hunc dilexerit, Deoq; ametur: quisquis oderit, Deum Hostem grauemq; is sentiat. In calle ueri Dominus ipsum deniq; Deducit, & praeit uiam. Si forte greßus turbet error lubricus (Vt labimur caeci indies) Non reprobatur, sed uigore numinis Mox subleuatus ambulat. Puer fui,quodcunq; uixi & hactenus Acui, senex fi consulo, Iusti relicti exempla nulla conspicor, Prolis nec eius turpiter Egentis. hic ut mutuo det,eroget, Multa in fideles pauperes:
units.tr: He also extends the rich inheritance of parents late to their posterity. Indeed, when misfortune thunders on every side with sad disasters, the goods and everything else of life that they need will be supplied to these people in abundance. The wicked will perish, as a voracious fire quickly consumes its victim. When the wicked man borrows, he repays nothing. But the righteous man, ever merciful to the poor, however sparingly he himself lives, helps, aids and lends. Hence he obtains such great and generous rewards that whoever loves him is loved by God, and whoever hates him will feel God as an enemy and a heavy one. I have been young and now am old, yet I have seen no example of the righteous forsaken, nor of his offspring begging shamefully; he lends and gives freely, and much to the faithful poor.

units.la: Liui[?] nepotes se tamen diuinitus Vident beari ditijs.
units.tr: Yet his grandchildren too, by divine favour, see themselves blessed with riches.

units.la: Quis haec optima, posita rectis artibus, Non praemia indagauerit?
units.tr: Who, having sought these best rewards by upright arts, would not look for the rewards?

units.la: Ah quisquis es sectare uerum, ut omnium Partem feras & munerum.
units.tr: Ah, whoever you are, follow the truth, so that you may bear a share of all the gifts.

units.la: Nam iustum & aequum semper est coram Deo, Suosq; nullus deserit:
units.tr: For the just and the equitable always stand before God, and he never deserts his own.

units.la: Custodit illos ad diem mundi ultimum, At semen impij eruit.
units.tr: He keeps them until the last day of the world, but he uproots the seed of the wicked.

units.la: Hereditate propria terram incolunt, Mundi stat haec dum machina.
units.tr: They dwell in the land as their own inheritance, for as long as this machine of the world stands.

units.la: Sapientia horum in ore semper delitet, Et lingua iustum personat.
units.tr: The wisdom of these men always lingers on their lips, and their tongue sounds forth what is just.

units.la: Diuina lex penetrale cordis afficit, Ne pes uacillet lubricus.
units.tr: The divine law touches the innermost heart, lest the foot slip and waver.

units.la: Iniustus omnem occasionem quaeritat, Vt innocentem exterminet:
units.tr: The unjust man seeks every occasion to destroy the innocent.

units.la: At qui tuetur hunc Deus libidini Non prostituet illum sua.
units.tr: But God protects the innocent man against their lust and will not hand him over to them.

units.la: Agitq; causam coram iniquo iudice, Ne praeualeat iniquitas.
units.tr: He pleads the cause before an unjust judge, lest injustice prevail.

units.la: Nunc ergo praestolare numen, & uiam Sectare ueri iugiter:
units.tr: Now therefore wait upon the Lord, and continually follow the way of truth.

units.la: Et reuehet[?] te Dominus, ut terram incolens Cernas malorum excidium.
units.tr: And the Lord will bring you back, so that, dwelling in the land, you may see the destruction of the wicked.

units.la: Vidi scelestum laureae instar consitae Trepidantis ad limphae alueum,
units.tr: I saw a wicked man, like a laurel planted by the bank of a trembling stream, lifting himself up,

units.la: Sese efferentem: cumq; transirem,en decor Et splendor hic euanuit. Quæsiui,& inuenire nusquam gloriæ Quiui caducæ imaginem. Mane innocens,uita scelus: namq; exitus Tandem sequetur te bonus, Qui durus impios manet: nam gaudia Clauduntur horum lacrymis. In rebus arctis forte munimen pijs Diuina uirtus excubat, Præsens & omne horum auferet periculum, Qui cuncta ad illum conferunt.
units.tr: and as I passed by, behold, his beauty and splendour vanished. I sought, and could nowhere find the image of his fleeting glory. Remain innocent, live righteously; for the end will follow you as good, while it awaits the impious harshly, since their joys are shut up in tears. In narrow straits, divine power keeps watch as a defence for the pious; present, it will remove all danger from those who refer everything to him.

units.tr: PSALM XXXVII.

units.la: Νανρῆ[?] νσνρῆσιν[?] χαμαί[?]λις, ἢ θρωσηόντεσιν[?] ἴγεῖς[?]· ἀντιλίπ[?] σώφρων, ἀνδρῶν ἀγάπημα λιπαίων[?], ἠλβοιο ἱερέοσων[?] πολυχρύσου[?] ἀταθαλιόντων[?]· λιάνων[?] γὰρ ἡ[?] ἡείγμ[?]' ὁ θεὸς, τῶν δὲ ἱερᾶτος αὐτὴν[?] ἐα[?] χαλεψάμενος μινύθα[?] ὡς ὀβειμοσφυγὴ[?] εἰναρέτης αὐδρας θεὸς ἐγω[?], ἠδὲ ἡ λήθη λαιροῖς ἀφηγέμενα[?], τῶν δ' ἐν ἐπιδλοντες[?] ὡσε[?] οἱ ἀαθαρροὶ γνώμεν[?], τῶντι ἰστίμ[?]' ἐμπιδλον ὡς[?] ἐν δὲ ἀνηπαθίαις σφίσιν ἡδεῖς ἀσχος ἀνάγκη[?], ὅτε βαρὺς θανάτῳ[?] ἰλινδωνον[?] λιμὸς ἐποίσει[?]· ἀλλ' ἐχθαίροντες τὸν λύσιον, ἡδὲ νοσοῦντες λυγρὰ, λακηῶς ἀπολλύντα[?] ὁμῶς τῷ πλοντι ἀνημῷ[?] ἐν λακηνισθεντι φλογέρας[?] ἐνι νυρπαιαίσιν[?]· πολλὰ δανείσασθαι λαβ' ἑκάστην αὐδρας ὁρῶντες οὐχ ὁσίως, μηδὲν τε λακοφράδιαις ἀποτίναι[?]· οἷς δὲ δικαιοσύνη φίλη ἐπλετο ὀλιόμοιρος[?], τοιαδὲ[?] ἐν ὁδὸν εἴῳς ἐγὼ ἔμον[?]· ὡς ὁ θεὸς φιλίᾳ ἑαθόροι μεγένεσιν[?] σύοιησι[?] γαίης νυροφόρω τῆς, ἀλλ' ὡς ἡν ἀποφυγέσιν[?] πεφρίζης χαίρει ἐντάμεναι[?] ἥντε ἀσνάρα[?] βήματα ἰθύνει θεὸς ὕπιος ὀρθοπολύντων[?]· ἀτραπιτοῖς τῶν γὰρ ἀγάλλεται[?]· ἢν δὲ πέσωσιν πλήμονες[?], ἀν' αἰεὶ ἀολιχοῖσιν ἐν ἀληθεσι[?] λιέντας[?] ἀλλὰ λακηῶν χεὶρ ὀφᾶς ἐξῆρπασε[?] πατρὸς ἐῶς[?] ἐν νεότητος ἐμῆς ἀχθι γήρας ὑπὸτ' ὀπωπα[?] πασθομένας ἀγανήσιν ἐφμοδύνῃ θεοῖο νόσφι βοηθεῖας χαλεπῶσιν ἀμηχανίησιν.
units.tr: The righteous man is wise, and his tongue speaks judgement; the law of his God is in his heart, and his steps do not slip. The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to slay him, but the Lord will not leave him in his hand nor let him be condemned when he is judged. Better is the little that the righteous has than the great wealth of many wicked men. The arms of the wicked will be broken, but the Lord upholds the righteous. The wicked borrows and does not repay, but the righteous is merciful and gives; those who are blessed by the Lord shall inherit the land, and those who are cursed by him shall be cut off. The steps of a good man are ordered by the Lord, and he delights in his way; though he fall, he shall not be cast down, for the Lord holds his hand. I have been young and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken nor his seed begging bread, though they are sorely pressed without help from God.

units.la: τέρσεδ' ἡλί' ἀπόλυς αὐτίσαμ ταιΐλα λίνα[?]ὺς[?] ἴσεχαρίζομενος ἰχθ' ἀπάχλυ ὁ Διαλέπης[?], ὁ μὲν ὑληρονόμυς ἐλλαψέ τι ἐνδιαπαύήσας[?], ἀλλὰ ἡ αὐτοῖσιν τόσα ἔστεται, ὅσ' ἐθέλωσιν συλλογίναι θεῷ ἁγίῳ γενέα ἐσσομεέναι τύρεννον ἵεμενος βιότῳ συλλίμονος, ἀλλ' ἀσύχῳ, ἀσπάτω χρὴ' ἤθεα, ἀσεβίλη τε, ἰδὲ λαπίης ἀποχαΐζδω ἀορρώταςα ταϊόνς[?], ὅτι Αἰνλω ἀγαπᾶν ὁ μήποτε ἐγνακαλέψα λύσεος οἱντίρμων ἀγαθῆς ἡ σώφρονας ἀνδρας[?], ὧν ταῖλες ταϊλλων ὡς ταῦτ' ἀῶνα φυλάξει[?], ἐν βάθρῳ ἀσεβὴν ἀπολέσας ἐξολέσας[?] ὅτω γὰρ βασιλῆϊ θεῷ φίλον ἐστὶ ἡ ἔγαυ[?], ἀδίμα ρείζοντας ἰχτέχαν γλῶ ὑμάτα ταὐτά ἐμπεξήπει συσεβέωρ σοφὴν φομάτιοσι[?], Αἰνλω[?] γλῶσσ' αὐτῶν λαλέα, φαναρῶς τε ψυδος ἰλέγχα[?], ἀιῷν ἐπιτυμίη πιστὴ ἐπιτάρροθος ἔσα τάτῳ συλλιάα ἰραλίης συτάλματα θεὼ[?], τρίνη' ὀλιδόντας πόλας αὐτῶν ἡν ἡγν ἰλυδ[?] τὰς δ' ἐκῆν λοχόωσι ἀλικοὶ ἐτάμῳ ὀξεὶ χαλκῷ ἓ σφιμ ὑφαίνωσιν διαβάλλοντες τιν' ὀἴῳ[?] ὃ μαὶ τῶν δ' ὀφελος λόγῳ ἀξιος ἔσεθ' ὅπως ἀὶ[?] ἀνσμενίωνῃς βίαιρ ὁ θεὸς ἡ χεῖρας ἀλάλνα[?] ἐπ' ἰχθρῶν ἐεφαλὰς ψῦν Αἰνυοὶλιν ἀποπέμπα[?], τῷ ῥαθεῷ ἐπέχειρ θέλε μόνῳ· τοῖ' ἐπίταγμα ἰντελέσας, χ' ὅτω θέοθεμ ὑλέος ὑραν ὑξα[?] ἀς μίν' ἀρβεύτος γάρ ἔνι τυλυβοτέρη[?],
units.tr: Do not be vexed because of evildoers, nor envy those who work iniquity; for they shall soon wither like the grass and fade like the green herb. Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and feed on his faithfulness. Delight yourself also in the Lord, and he shall give you the desires of your heart. Commit your way to the Lord and trust in him, and he shall bring it to pass. He shall bring forth your righteousness as the light and your judgement as the noonday. Rest in the Lord and wait patiently for him; do not fret because of him who prospers in his way, nor because of the man who brings wicked devices to pass. Cease from anger, forsake wrath, and do not fret, which only leads to evil. For evildoers shall be cut off, but those who wait upon the Lord shall inherit the land. Yet the wicked shall be no more; you shall look well at his place and he shall not be there. But the meek shall inherit the land and delight themselves in abundance of peace.

units.tr: 35 Just as a man who is well-fed and flourishing (as the green bay tree) spreads out, I saw the ungodly man exalted and spreading himself like the cedars of Lebanon; 36 yet he passed away, and behold, he was no more; I sought him, but he could not be found. 37 Mark the blameless man and behold the upright, for there is a future for the man of peace. 38 But the transgressors shall perish together, and the posterity of the wicked shall be cut off. 39 But the salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, who is their strength in the time of trouble; the Lord helps them and delivers them from the wicked. 40 For all who are being rescued have one hope, the God who is their deliverer.

units.la: Simon Stenius.
units.tr: Simon Stenius.

units.la: PSALMVS XXXVII.
units.tr: PSALM XXXVII.

units.la: Quid tua mens frustra vanas consurgit in iras, Prospera dū passim fata malignus habet?
units.tr: Why does your mind vainly rise in empty wrath, while the wicked everywhere enjoy prosperous fates?

units.la: Non decet insuetis placitis foedare tribunal, Judicij cum non copia facta tibi est.
units.tr: It is not fitting to defile the tribunal with unaccustomed judgements, since no opportunity of judging has been given to you.

units.la: Stat sua cuiq; dies: posita est sua meta malignis, Cum pessum, herbosi graminis instar, eant.
units.tr: Each man's day is fixed; a limit is set for the wicked, when they perish like the grass of the field.

units.la: Vita mali bullae similis, quae flumine surgit, In nihilum subito, quod fuit ante, ruens.
units.tr: The life of the wicked is like a bubble that rises from the river, suddenly collapsing into the nothing it was before.

units.la: Cede Deo: in Iova solo tibi fixa quiescat Spes, & fidenti pectore munus obi.
units.tr: Yield to God: let your hope rest fixed in Jehovah alone, and perform your duty with a trusting heart.

units.la: Tempora non deerunt placidæ optatissima uitæ, Nec satur acceptam sollicitabis opem.
units.tr: Times will not be lacking, most desired for a peaceful life, nor, once satisfied, will you vex the help you have received.

units.la: Sit sanctum Numen tibi cor, sit summa voluptas, Atq; ultro, cupida mente, petita feres.
units.tr: Let the holy Godhead be your heart, let it be your highest delight, and you will bear away with eager mind what you seek of your own accord.

units.la: Ipse Pater: patrij non est desertor amoris, Natorum haud uentis uota precesq; dabit.
units.tr: The Father himself is no deserter of paternal love; he will not refuse his children their prayers and vows.

units.la: Huic munus committe tuum coeptosq; labores, Et pulcrum, iusto iudice, stabit opus.
units.tr: Commit to him your task and your toilsome efforts, and the fine work will stand, with the just Judge as its judge.

units.la: Dirigit is gressus hominum: uia lubrica nobis: Nil facimus, nostro non faciente Deo.
units.tr: He directs the steps of men; the way is slippery for us: we do nothing, without God doing it for us.

units.la: Ioua Deus facit, & faciet: spem concipe firmam: Hic opus, hic, nutu diriget, omne, suo.
units.tr: Jehovah God makes and will make: conceive a firm hope: he will direct every work by his nod.

units.la: Hinc quamuis rectè factorum conscius absit, Non tamen, æterna nocte, silebit opus.
units.tr: Hence, although the one conscious of rightly done deeds is absent, the work will not, in eternal night, be silent.

units.la: Nam tandem in lucem uenient tua facta, tuisq; Pro meritis, iusta, præmia, lege, feres.
units.tr: For at last your deeds will come into the light, and for your merits you will receive and read just rewards.

units.la: Non tantum in tenebris Solis iubar emicat, orbi Vt tuus æterno iudice stabit honos.
units.tr: Not only in darkness does the sun's radiance shine on the world, so that your honour will stand with the eternal Judge.

units.la: Fer patiens quodcunq; potes: sic tempore recto Optata dabitur prosperitate frui.
units.tr: Bear patiently whatever you can: thus in the right time you will be given to enjoy the desired prosperity.

units.la: Ne moueat mentem, quòd floreat impius, actu Externo ac curæ se probet esse Deo.
units.tr: Let it not disturb your mind that the wicked flourish; by their outward conduct they show themselves to be a care to God.

units.la: Dispereat quisquis successu iudicat uno, Arbitria atq; fugit iudicis æqua sequi.
units.tr: Let perish whoever judges by one success alone, and shuns the just judgements of the Judge to follow them.

units.la: Exitus acta probat. Positam timet impius urnam: Aspera non horret fata subire pius.
units.tr: The outcome proves the deeds. The wicked man fears the urn set before him; the pious man does not shrink from undergoing harsh fates.

units.la: Dantur amara pijs, sed puri pocula uini: Cum pice, cū nitro, restat amurca malis. siste pedem. Hæc nil sors aliud quàm graminis her- Mane viges, media, marcida, nocte, cades. (ba [?] est, Tempus erit, quando vestigia nulla superbū Cernes, & læta mente, Fuere, feres. Sedes fixa piis perduri roboris instar, Quod non ventorum vis inimica movet. Idcirco optata felices pace fruentur, Nec contra poterit bella movere malus. Impius arma capit: Deus at conatibus obstans Consuevit forti frangere tela manu. Dentibus infrendens tensum capit impius arcum, Atq; parat stricto feruidus ense necem. Subridens Dominus metam præfigit, & ultrà Iustorum in fraudem non sinit ire malum. Infelix miles ferrum in sua viscera stringit, Inq; suum pectus spicula torquet iners. Eximia est virtus thesaurum quærere, & illo Concessa (ut par est) conditione frui. Quærit opes expers iusti: sed negligit æquum; Debitaq; idcirco præmia egenus habet. Sufficit exiguum naturæ. Est rectior usus Qui pura exiguas mente paravit opes. Namq; nives velut Solis rapiuntur ab æstu; Non secus, iniustè partus acervus, abit. Iniusti Deus est vindex, atq; osor[?] iniqui: Conatum iniusti nec sinit esse ratum. Novit Jova dies iustorum, tempora novit: Non ultra metam sæva pericla nocent.
units.tr: Bitter draughts are given to the pious, but the cups of pure wine; with pitch and nitre, the lees remain for the wicked. Stop your foot. This fate is nothing other than that of the grass and herb: in the morning it flourishes, at midday it withers, at night it falls. There will be a time when you will see no trace of the proud man, and with a glad mind you will bear it. The seat of the pious is fixed like a hardy oak, which the hostile force of the winds does not move. Therefore the blessed will enjoy the desired peace, nor can the wicked stir up war against them. The wicked man takes up arms; but God, opposing his attempts, is accustomed to break their weapons with a strong hand. Gnashing his teeth, the wicked man seizes the bent bow, and burning, prepares death with drawn sword. The Lord, smiling, sets a limit, and does not let the evil go further to the deceit of the just. The unhappy soldier thrusts the sword into his own entrails, and the helpless one turns his darts against his own breast. It is an excellent virtue to seek treasure and, on the condition granted (as is right), to enjoy it. The one lacking righteousness seeks wealth but neglects what is fair, and so the needy man receives the rewards that are owed him. What is small suffices for nature; more right is the use of one who with a pure mind has gained modest wealth. For as snows are snatched away by the heat of the sun, so the heap unjustly gained departs. God is the avenger of the unjust and the hater of the iniquitous; he does not allow the attempt of the unjust to stand. Jehovah knows the days of the just, knows their times: harsh dangers do not harm beyond the limit.

units.la: Nititur aduersus mala iustus palmitis instar, Conatusq; ideo præmia lætus habet.
units.tr: The just man strives against evils like a palm shoot, and so he joyfully has the rewards of his efforts.

units.la: At quisquis dubitat venerari Numen honore, Is merito spretus fert sine honore dies.
units.tr: But whoever doubts to worship the Godhead with honour is rightly rejected, and bears his days without honour.

units.la: Stat pro lege sua Deus: & cadit impius, ara Incensa veluti victima opima perit.
units.tr: God stands by his law, and the wicked man falls; like a burnt sacrificial victim he perishes.

units.la: Contrahere alterius non ære veretur iniquus: Mutua, sed iusta, reddere, lance, negat.
units.tr: The wicked man does not fear to borrow with another's money, but refuses to repay what is owed, just and full weight.

units.la: Iusticiæ cultor largiri sentit egeno Æquum, nec dando plurima poscit opem.
units.tr: The cultivator of justice perceives that he gives what is fair to the needy, and in giving he does not ask for much help.

units.la: Quisquis enim sentit Superorum Numen amicum, Non facile à placidis sedibus ille ruit.
units.tr: For whoever perceives the Godhead of the heavenly ones to be friendly does not easily fall from his peaceful seat.

units.la: At quem persequitur consumens flamma Tonantis, In nihilum, incensi cespitis instar, abit.
units.tr: But he whom the consuming flame of the Thunderer pursues vanishes into nothing, like a burnt sod.

units.la: Ipse Deus iusto ductor: non tramite aberrat, Mandatum tanto qui duce currit iter.
units.tr: God himself is the leader of the just: he does not stray from the path, for whoever runs his course under such a leader does not go astray.

units.la: Plurima vitæ obstant hominum: at nil fraudibus illis Efficitur, nostro, nil, prohibente Deo.
units.tr: Many obstacles of human life stand in the way, but nothing is achieved by those frauds, nothing, with God forbidding it for us.

units.la: Ecce senex, uixi dum fata Deusq; sinebant: Non sensi auxilium sollicitare pios.
units.tr: Behold, an old man: I have lived as long as the fates and God allowed, and I have not seen the pious having to beg for help.

units.la: Pulsari à iusto non diuitis ostia uidi, Vel sanctum, humanam poscere, semen, opem.
units.tr: I have not seen the doors of the rich pushed shut against the just, nor a holy seed asking for human aid.

units.la: Diuidit in medium sanctus sibi parta, nec ullum Hæredem, uacuum munere, abire finit.
units.tr: The holy man divides his own goods in the midst, and lets no heir depart empty of gift.

units.la: Vsq; adeo pietas sentit sua præmia: donum Perpetuum sanctæ fert probitatis amor.
units.tr: So far does piety perceive its rewards: the love of holy uprightness bears a perpetual gift.

units.la: Ergo quisquis amas optata pace potiri, Sit iusti & recti maxima cura tibi.
units.tr: Therefore, whoever loves to obtain peace as he desires, let the greatest care of the just and the right be yours.

units.la: Non unquā subeant castum scelera improba pectus Iniusti, nec mens, facta nefanda probet.
units.tr: Let wicked crimes never enter the chaste breast of the unjust, nor let the mind approve unspeakable deeds.

units.la: Gaudet quippe Deus syncero pectore: & inde Tristia (non falsò) fata superbus habet.
units.tr: For God rejoices in a sincere heart, and therefore the proud man has sad fates (and not falsely so).

units.la: Fas numerare pijs longæua ætate nepotes: At primo sentit, funera, flore, malus.
units.tr: It is lawful for the pious to count their grandchildren in long old age; but the wicked man sees funerals at the first bloom.

units.la: Iusto iusta Deo sunt curæ: & cultor honesti Præmia in innumera posteritate capit.
units.tr: Righteous things are a concern to the just God, and the cultivator of honesty receives rewards in countless posterity.

units.la: Est præsens Numen sanctis, & robore firmat, Incutiant ne quem, sæua pericla, metum.
units.tr: The present Godhead is with the holy and strengthens them with firmness, so that harsh dangers may not strike fear into anyone.

units.la: Nam vt lingua sacrâm sonat imperterrita legem: Sic unum mentes Numen honore colunt.
units.tr: For as the tongue undaunted sounds the sacred law, so minds honour the one God alone.

units.la: Hinc non insidias horrent scelerumq; tribunal, Nec fera peruersi iudicis ora timent.
units.tr: Hence they do not dread ambushes and the tribunal of crimes, nor do they fear the savage face of a perverse judge.

units.la: Quippe Dei secum referunt in corde fauorem, Quo, facilè expirat, corda calente, timor.
units.tr: For they carry in their heart the favour of God, by which fear is easily driven out when the heart is warm.

units.la: Tu ne cede malis, sed contrà audentior ito: Non procul est, durum qui releuabit onus.
units.tr: You, do not yield to evils, but go on more boldly: he who will lighten the hard burden is not far off.

units.la: Te tua tunc, Superis charum, super æthera virtus Tollet, & innocuo corde patebit honos.
units.tr: Then your virtue, dear to the heavenly ones, will lift you above the sky, and honour will lie open to a harmless heart.

units.la: Fide Deo, & dabitur manifesta in luce uidere, Post paulò, pessum, funditùs, ire, malum.
units.tr: Trust God, and you will be given to see plainly in the light, after a little while, the wicked go headlong to ruin.

units.la: Vidi ego surgentis, florentem, palmitis instar Iniustum, exiguo tempore nullus erat.
units.tr: I have seen the wicked man, flourishing like a rising palm shoot; in a short time he was nowhere.

units.la: Non uana est Domini tantis cum uiribus ira: In nihilum, Iouæ quem premit ira, ruit. Profeßo[?] Deus est, iustos qui curat, & ampla Munera, syncera pro pietate refert.
units.tr: The wrath of the Lord is not vain with such powers: he whom the wrath of Jehovah presses falls into nothing. God, who cares for the just, is a God who keeps his word, and repays great gifts for sincere piety.

units.la: Est etiam Numen, iusto quo uindice, iustas Iniustus pœnas impietatis habet.
units.tr: There is also a Godhead, by whose vindication of the just the unjust bears the penalties of his impiety.

units.la: Ne trepida, quamuis fremat horridus Orcus & Or- Namq; piis, Ioua, nil, prohibente, nocent. (bis:
units.tr: Do not tremble, though the dreadful Orcus roars and the world with it; for nothing harms the pious, Jehovah, with God forbidding it.

units.la: Concipe spem firmam: Deus est qui corda bonorum Laudat, & iratus facta superba notat.
units.tr: Conceive a firm hope: God is he who praises the hearts of the good, and, angered, marks proud deeds.

units.la: Ille Deus, Deus ille suum non deserit agmen: Iudicia hic iusto tempore iusta dabit.
units.tr: That God, that God does not desert his band: here he will give just judgements at the right time.

units.la: Gregorius Frisch Vratisl. Silesius.
units.tr: Gregorius Frisch, of Breslau, Silesian.

units.la: PSALMUS XXXVII. Carmine Heroico redditus.
units.tr: Psalm 37. Rendered in heroic verse.

units.la: Iniustos rebus uideas si forte secundis Elatos, nimioq; animum turgescere fastu: Ne tibi mens tristem mox efferuescat in iram.
units.tr: If perchance you see the unjust lifted up by prosperous circumstances, and their spirit swelling with excessive pride, do not let your mind soon boil over into gloomy anger.

units.la: Nam uelut herba uirens modo, post arescit, & o- Succisa subito amittit radice uigorem; Utq; per incultos marcescunt gramina campos Agricolæ desecta manu: sic tota malorum Successu defuncta breui mox turba peribit.
units.tr: For like grass that is green for a moment and then withers, cut down suddenly and losing its vigour from the root, and as grass wilts across untilled fields once cut by the farmer's hand, so the whole crowd of evils, once its success is spent, will soon perish in a short time.

units.la: Quin potius confide Deo, uitijsq; relictis, Quæ bona sunt semper studio sectare fideli, Incola sic terræ secura pace frueris.
units.tr: Rather, trust in God, and with vices abandoned, always pursue with faithful zeal what is good; thus, as a dweller in the land, you will enjoy peace in security.

units.la: Nulla uelit, praeterue Deum mens gaudia quaerat, Sic precibus potiere tuis, optataq; uotis
units.tr: Let no mind wish for other joys, but let it seek its delight in God alone; thus you will obtain by your prayers and your desired wishes all that you bear.

units.la: Cunctaferes. Quod si mentem dolor urget, in illum Exonera curasq; tuas tristemq; dolorem: Diriget ille tuos obscuro in tramite gressus.
units.tr: But if grief presses upon your mind, unload onto him your cares and your sad sorrow: he will direct your steps along the dark path.

units.la: Quinetiam ius ille tuum de nocte reductum Omnibus exponet terris, ut fulgeat illud, Fulget ut in medio consistens Phoebus olympo.
units.tr: Moreover, he will bring your right forth, drawn back from the night, and display it to all lands, so that it shines as Phoebus shines when he stands in mid-heaven.

units.la: Interea quaecunq; premant te aduersa, sileto Expectaq; Deum, neq; te fortuna malorum Commoueat, iustamue adigat dolor ullus in iram,
units.tr: Meanwhile, whatever adversities press upon you, be silent and wait for God; let neither the chance of evils move you, nor any pain drive you into just anger.

units.la: Sed potius turbantem animum compescefurorem, Pelle iram, nec te scelerum contagia laedant.
units.tr: But rather, to calm your troubled mind, drive out wrath; let not the contagions of crimes harm you.

units.la: Nam genus iniusti totum excindetur, at omnis In Domino qui sperat opes & regna tenebit.
units.tr: For the whole race of the unjust will be rooted out, but all who hope in the Lord will hold wealth and kingdoms.

units.la: Mox etenim infanda misere cum stirpe peribit Impius: inquires ubi sit, quo euaserit, & non Illius in tota extabunt uestigia terra.
units.tr: Soon indeed the impious man will perish wretchedly, with his unspeakable stock. You will ask where he is and whither he has escaped, and no traces of him will remain in the whole land.

units.la: Contra humili quicunq; Deum pietate timebunt, Hos terrae efficiet dominos, & pace beabit.
units.tr: On the contrary, whoever fear God with humble piety, he will make them lords of the land and bless them with peace.

units.la: Multa parat nocitura pio scelerato, & omni Fraude tumet, rabidamq; ostendit dentibus iram:
units.tr: He prepares many things to harm the pious; the wicked man swells with every fraud and shows raging anger with his teeth.

units.la: At Deus ex alto cernens mortalia, secum Ridet, & exitij illius bene praeuidet horam.
units.tr: But God from on high, seeing mortal things, laughs to himself and foresees well the hour of his destruction.

units.la: Ille quidem gladium iustorū in ulnera stringit Ille suum totis incuruat uiribus arcum:
units.tr: He indeed draws his sword against the wounds of the just; he bends his bow with all his strength.

units.la: Sed bene habet, quo fata alijs indigna minatur, In sua conuersum desiget pectora ferrum, Et manibus subito trepidantibus excidet arcus.
units.tr: But it turns out well: the sword that he threatens against others with unworthy fates will be turned back and fixed in his own breast, and his bow will suddenly fall from his trembling hands.

units.la: Longè equidem iusti res parua, & munda supel- Diuitis est potior gazis, atq; ubere fundo. Concidet illius succisum robur, & omnis Copia non multis iterum male diffluet annis.
units.tr: Far better is the small possession of the righteous, and clean, than the treasures of the rich and their fertile estates. His strength, cut down, will fall, and all his abundance will again wretchedly dissolve in not many years.

units.la: Cursus enim vitæ iustorum, & summa dierum Nota Deo est, beat ille suos, prolemq; suorum, Non illis aliquem incutient aduersa pudorem, Nutriet hos ubi dira fames mala plurima terris Inferet, & misera mortales tabe necabit.
units.tr: For the course of the lives of the just and the sum of their days is known to God; he blesses his own and their offspring. Adversity will not bring shame upon them; when dire famine brings many evils upon the lands, it will nourish them, and it will destroy mortals with wretched decay.

units.la: At quicunq; Deum offendent, ceu fumus in auras Fertur, ubi rapidis absumpta est victima flammis, Sic subita, & nulli miseranda morte peribunt.
units.tr: But whoever offend God, as smoke is carried into the air when the victim is consumed by rapid flames, so they will perish suddenly, with a death that none pities.

units.la: Semper egens & pauper erit, neq; debita soluet, Et miseros peraget sine luce & honoribus annos. Nunquam exhausta domus iusti, sed diuite uena Fundit opes, semper miseris succurrere gaudens; Idcirco stabili terras hic sorte tenebit, Euertiq; uidebit opes, & regna potentum.
units.tr: He will always be needy and poor, and will not pay what he owes, and he will spend wretched years without light and honours. The house of the just is never exhausted, but pours forth wealth from a rich vein, always rejoicing to help the wretched; therefore he will hold the lands here by a stable lot, and he will see the wealth and kingdoms of the powerful overturned.

units.la: Sed iusti Deus à lapsu vestigia seruat, Et quocunq; ferat gressus comitatur euntem, Quinetiam ne forte cadens simul occidat, illi Auxilium laturus adest, dextramq; iacenti Porrigit, atq; pedes nutantes robore firmat.
units.tr: But God preserves the steps of the just from falling, and wherever he goes he accompanies him as he walks. Moreover, lest perhaps he fall and perish at once, God is present to bring help, and he stretches out his right hand to the one lying down and strengthens his tottering feet.

units.la: Ipse ego me puerum memini, nunc tarda senectus Tota mihi raris circumdat tempora canis:
units.tr: I myself remember that I was a boy; now slow old age surrounds my temples entirely with sparse white hair.

units.la: Sed tamen ut primæ repetam incunabula vitæ, Non ego iustorum quenquam hæc ad tempora vidi Desertum, aut iusti genitam de sanguine prolem Exiguo pro pane fores pulsare potentum.
units.tr: Yet, to return to the cradle of my first life: I have not seen, down to these times, anyone of the just forsaken, nor the children born of the blood of the just begging at the doors of the powerful for a meagre bread.

units.la: 26 Immo etiam illius excipiet benedictio stirpem, Et quo plura dabit miseris, hoc plura relinquet.
units.tr: 26 Indeed, moreover, a blessing will receive his offspring, and the more he gives to the wretched, the more he will leave behind.

units.la: 27 Ergo agite a vitijs cunctis avertite mentem, Et toto, quodcunq; bonum est, inquirite sensu.
units.tr: 27 Therefore come, turn your mind away from all vices, and seek with your whole sense whatever is good.

units.la: 28 Iudicij Deus & recti custodit amantes: Rursus iniquorum gentem radicitus omnem Eruit, illarumq; vetat reuirescere stirpem.
units.tr: 28 God guards the lovers of judgment and of right; again he uproots every race of the wicked and forbids their stock to grow again.

units.la: 29 Verum habitanda pijs terræ pars optima cedet, Quam neq; vis illis unquam, neq; bella, nec hostis Auferet, & dulcem audebit turbare quietem.
units.tr: 29 But the best part of the land, to be inhabited by the pious, will fall to them; neither force nor wars nor an enemy will take it from them, nor dare to disturb their sweet quiet.

units.la: 30 Vera etenim iusti sapientia manat ab ore, Lingua quod est rectum profert, infixaq; cordi 31 Illius, lex sancta altis radicibus hæret. Hac duce non ullum metuent vestigia lapsum, Quamlibet horrendam minitentur cuncta ruinam.
units.tr: 30 For the true wisdom of the just flows from their mouth; their tongue utters what is right, and the holy law, fixed in their heart, 31 clings with deep roots. With this as their guide, their steps will fear no fall, however dreadful the ruin that everything threatens.

units.la: 32 Impius insidijs & fraude armatus, in illum Fertur, & exitium capto crudele minatur.
units.tr: 32 The impious man, armed with snares and fraud, rushes against the just and threatens cruel destruction to the one he has captured.

units.la: 33 Sed Deus insontem semper tegit, inq; frequenti Iudicio, iniusto damnatum a iudice, seruat.
units.tr: 33 But God always shelters the innocent, and in frequent judgment he preserves the one condemned by an unjust judge.

units.la: 34 Hunc igitur, quicunq; aliqua sub mole laboras, Expecta, dum te sublatum e puluere, tandem Hæredem efficiat terræ, videasq; malorum Exitia, & tristes secura mente ruinas.
units.tr: 34 Therefore, whoever you are that labours under some heavy burden, wait until God lifts you from the dust and at last makes you heir of the land, and you see with a secure mind the destructions of the wicked and their sad ruins.

units.la: His oculis, his, inquam, oculis, vidi ipse ferocem In morem viridis sese diffundere palmae. Vidi atq; obstupui: sed mox dum lumina verto, Respiciocq; virum, (dictu mirabile,) tantus Iampridem tumor in tenues evaserat auras, Nec corpus, nec erant vestigia corporis usquam. At iustum si nosse cupis bene: respice finem. Nam licet hic misere pressus gemat, attamen omnes Quos tulit excipiet tandem pars firma labores. At quibus impietas cordi est, scelerumq; libido, Horrendo simul exitio cum stirpe peribunt. Namq; salus iusti Deus est, & robur, ubi ingens Tempestas movet horrendos adversa tumultus, Tum vero auxiliator adest, & ab hoste superbo Eripit, incolumesq; suos per secula servat.
units.tr: With these eyes, I say, with these very eyes, I myself saw the fierce man spreading himself out like a green palm. I saw and was astonished; but soon, when I turned my eyes and looked back for the man (wonderful to tell), such a swelling had long since dissolved into thin air, and there was no body, nor any trace of a body anywhere. But if you wish to know the just well, look to the end. For although he groans here, wretchedly pressed, yet at last the steadfast part receives all the labours he has borne. But those whose heart is impiety and lust for crime will perish together with their stock in dreadful destruction. For the safety and strength of the just is God; when a huge tempest of adversity stirs up dreadful tumults, then indeed he is present as helper, and snatches his own from the proud enemy, and preserves them unharmed through the ages.

units.la: Ioannes Sanderus Saxo L.
units.tr: Johannes Sanderus, of Saxony, L.

units.la: PSALMVS XXXVII, carmine Sapphico conversus.
units.tr: PSALM XXXVII, turned into Sapphic verse.

units.la: INsolens rebus nimium secundis Si tibi afflicto toleranda turba est, Inuidum non te faciat, nec armet Liuor in iram.
units.tr: Though you are insolent in your overly favourable circumstances, if you must put up with a crowd of the afflicted, let envy not make you, nor let malice arm you to anger.

units.la: Nam uelut campi decus herba, languet, Gramen ut fibris moritur recisis: Sic repentina genus impiorum Morte peribit.
units.tr: For as the grass withers, the glory of the field, as turf dies when its roots are cut, so the race of the impious will perish in sudden death.

units.la: In Deo semper tua spes recumbat, Mente quod iustum est cupida sequaris, Nec tibi uictus, neq; pax, boniq; Copia deerit.
units.tr: Let your hope always rest in God; follow what is just with an eager mind, and neither food nor peace nor abundance of good things will be lacking to you.

units.la: In Deo tantum tua sit voluptas, Quicquid optaris dabit ille promptus, Nec diu incassum sinet ut fatiges Astra quaerelis.
units.tr: Let your delight be in God alone; he will readily give whatever you desire, and he will not allow you to wear yourself out in vain with complaints about the stars for long.

units.la: Hunc ducem uitae cupias, uiaeq;, Mentis hic curas releuabit aegrae, Res tuas solus reget, & beabit, Providus omnes.
units.tr: Desire him as the leader of your life and your way. He alone will relieve the cares of your sick mind, will rule your affairs, and, as the provident one, will make all of them happy.

units.la: Sistet in claram tua iura lucem, Facta quo cunctis manifesta terris Luceant, ceu Sol medio refulgens Lucet olympo.
units.tr: He will set your rights in a clear light, so that the facts, made manifest to all lands, may shine, as the sun shining in the middle of the sky shines.

units.la: Nulla sperantem mora te fatiget, Sed silens mentis superes tumultus, Improbae nec sors moueat dolorem Prospera turbae.
units.tr: Let no delay weary you while you hope, but silently overcome the tumults of your mind; nor let the prosperous lot of the wicked stir up grief in you.

units.la: Mitte, quae mentem male turbat irant, Comprime insanos animi tumultus, Nec dolor tantum generet furorem, Ut mala patres.
units.tr: Put aside the anger that troubles the mind badly; restrain the mad tumults of the spirit, and let not grief generate such fury as the wicked fathers did.

units.la: Funditus cœtus pereunt malorum, At quibus spes est Deus, hi perenni Pace felices, sua possidebunt Regna per orbem.
units.tr: The assemblies of the wicked perish utterly; but those who have God as their hope will be happy in lasting peace and will possess their kingdoms throughout the world.

units.la: Impij cursu modico fruuntur, Inde ad æternas abeunt tenebras, Transiens quæres hominem, locumq;, Non erit usquam.
units.tr: The impious enjoy a brief course, and then they pass into eternal darkness; you will seek the man and the place, and he will be nowhere.

units.la: Sed pij quamuis inopes bonorum, Attamen terras, & opes tenebunt, Semper & festa sine lite & armis Pace fruentur.
units.tr: But the pious, though they lack good things, will nevertheless hold the lands and the wealth, and they will enjoy peace always, feasts without strife or arms.

units.la: Impius iusto mala dum minatur, Liuidos dentes acuit, fremitq;, Sed Deus tantum interea furorem Ridet ab alto.
units.tr: While the impious man threatens harm to the just, he whets his teeth and roars, but God meanwhile laughs at his fury from on high.

units.la: In pios strictis gladijs feruntur, Vulnus intenso minitantur arcu, Nempe quò stratos inopesq; diro Funere mactent.
units.tr: They advance against the pious with drawn swords, threaten the wound with a tightly strung bow, namely to slay the fallen and the needy with a dreadful death.

units.la: Ictibus uersis sua corda figent, Et suis ipsi gladijs peribunt, Arcus illorum simul, & sagittæ Comminuentur.
units.tr: With their own blows turned against them, they will pierce their own hearts, and they themselves will perish by their own swords; their bows and arrows will be broken together.

units.la: Copiæ certè modicæ piorum Diuitum gazis opibusq; præstant, Quamlibet multo domus impiorum Splendeat auro.
units.tr: Indeed, the modest resources of the pious are better than the treasures and riches of the rich, however much the house of the impious may glitter with gold.

units.la: Nam Deus fastu nimio feroces Deprimet tandem, minuetq; vires, At suo reddet stabilem piorum Numine sortem.
units.tr: For God will at last cast down the proud in their excessive arrogance and diminish their strength, but he will give the pious a firm lot by his divine power.

units.la: Terminum his vitæ statuit, diesq; Usq; ad extremam numerat senectam, Atq; inexhausto sinit ut fruantur Fonte bonorum.
units.tr: He has set a limit to their life and counts their days up to extreme old age, and he lets them enjoy the inexhaustible fount of good things.

units.la: Non malis presi uarijs satiscent, Spes nec illorum pudefiet unquam[?], Nec sames totis metuenda terris Opprimet illos.
units.tr: Pressed by no various evils, they will not grow weary; their hope will never be put to shame, nor will famine, to be feared throughout all lands, overwhelm them.

units.la: Rursus iniusti genus interibit, Et Deum quisquis vitijs[?] lacesset, Illius tandem referet fugaces Gloria fumos.
units.tr: Again, the race of the unjust will perish; and whoever provokes God by his vices, at last the glory of the fleeting smoke will return to him.

units.la: Semper est iusto super unde donet, Semper iniustis comes est egestas: Mutuum sumunt avidi, nec unquam[?] Soluere curant.
units.tr: There is always something from which the just man can give; want is always a companion to the unjust: the greedy borrow, and never care to repay.

units.la: At quibus præsto sauor est supremi Numinis, terræ domini manebunt, Huius expertes: penitus recisa Stirpe peribunt.
units.tr: But those who have the favour of the Supreme Deity at hand will remain lords of the land; excluded from this, the stock cut off utterly will perish.

units.la: Ille iustorum regit usq; gressus, Ille cunctarum comes est viarum, Illius cunctos prohibere prompta est Dextera lapsus.
units.tr: He always guides the steps of the just; he is the companion of all ways; his right hand is ready to keep all of them from stumbling.

units.la: Et puer uixi & senui, nec unquam[?] A Deo iustum memini relictum, Voce nec prolem querula piorum Poscere panem.
units.tr: I was a boy and have grown old, and I do not recall ever having seen the just forsaken by God, nor the children of the pious begging for bread with a plaintive voice.

units.la: Pauperum cunctis miseretur horis, Mutuum si quis petat, ecce praesto est. Ditat haec longa serie futuram Copia prolem.
units.tr: He has mercy on the poor at all hours; if anyone asks for a loan, behold, it is at hand. Through a long line of descendants, abundance enriches the offspring to come.

units.la: Sed caue ne te uitijs solutum, Dira peruertat scelerum libido. Sic Deo semper peragés quietam Vindice vitam.
units.tr: But take care lest the dire lust of crimes, once you are freed from vices, overturn you. Thus you will always lead a quiet life with God as your protector.

units.la: Nam Deus iusti Deus est & aequi, Et probat iusti cupidos & aequi: Hos in aeternum tegit, at malorum Agmina delet.
units.tr: For God is the God of the just and the equitable, and he approves the just and equitable who desire him; he shelters these for ever, but he destroys the hosts of the wicked.

units.la: Terra sed iusto spaciosa cedet, Et quidem cunctis habitanda seclis. Illius iustum, sapiensq;, semper Lingua loquetur.
units.tr: But the earth will yield its spacious lands to the just, and it is to be inhabited by all ages. The tongue of the just and wise man will always speak of his justice.

units.la: Qui Dei legum studio feruntur, Hasq; non ficta pietate seruant: Non cadent, quamuis subitam minentur Cuncta ruinam.
units.tr: Those who are carried along by zeal for the laws of God, and keep them with no feigned piety, will not fall, though all things threaten sudden ruin.

units.la: Impius iusti sitiens cruoris, Tendit occultos laqueos eunti,
units.tr: The impious man, thirsting for the blood of the just, lays hidden snares for the one who passes by,

units.la: Donec arentes riget innocenti
units.tr: until his parched jaws are wet

units.la: Sanguine fauces.
units.tr: with the blood of the innocent.

units.la: Sed Deus tantum reprimit furorem,
units.tr: But God restrains his fury only so far,

units.la: Nec capi dextra sinit hunc cruenta,
units.tr: and does not allow the bloody man to be caught by his right hand,

units.la: Et sub iniusto quoties laborat
units.tr: and as often as he labours before an unjust

units.la: Iudice, seruat.
units.tr: judge, he preserves him.

units.la: Vrgeant si te mala multa, spera,
units.tr: If many evils press upon you, hope,

units.la: Et Dei iustas uenerare leges,
units.tr: and revere the just laws of God,

units.la: Illius tandem quoq; te iacentem
units.tr: and at last his right hand will also raise you

units.la: Dextra leuabit.
units.tr: when you lie prostrate.

units.la: Portio terræ tibi magna cedet,
units.tr: A large portion of the land will fall to you;

units.la: Hanc in æternum tua stirps tenebit.
units.tr: your stock will hold it for ever.

units.la: At malos contrà scelerum uidebis
units.tr: But on the contrary you will see the wicked

units.la: Pendere pœnas.
units.tr: paying the penalties of their crimes.

units.la: Impios lauro similes uirenti
units.tr: I have seen the impious raise their lofty heads to heaven,

units.la: Ferre conspexi capita alta cœlo.
units.tr: like the green laurel.

units.la: Sed breui tantos reprimi Gigantes
units.tr: But I saw such giants

units.la: Tempore uidi.
units.tr: checked in a short time.

units.la: Iustus, & ueri studiosus æqui,
units.tr: The just man, and one zealous for true equity,

units.la: Cladibus multis licet hic prematur,
units.tr: though here he is oppressed by many disasters,

units.la: Attamen curis semel his solutus
units.tr: nevertheless, once freed from these cares,

units.la: Pace fruetur.
units.tr: will enjoy peace.

units.la: At quibus nec ius pietasq; cordi est,
units.tr: But those to whom neither right nor piety is dear

units.la: Exitu certè misero peribunt,
units.tr: will certainly perish in a wretched end;

units.la: Vna lux illos tumidos uidebit,
units.tr: one light will see those swollen with pride,

units.la: Vna iacentes.
units.tr: one light will see them lying low.

units.la: Nam salus curæ est Domino piorum, Asserit iustos, leuat innocentes, Et laborantes animas potenti Robore firmat.
units.tr: For the Lord cares for the salvation of the pious; he vindicates the just, lifts up the innocent, and strengthens the labouring souls with powerful might.

units.la: Eruet iustos quibus impiorum Imminet passim scelerata turba, Et sinet vitam placida per omnem Pace fruantur.
units.tr: He will rescue the just, over whom the wicked crowd of the impious hangs everywhere, and he will allow them to live and enjoy peace throughout all their days.
